## Unmet Criterion
[P2] AC-9 built-in default panel uses provider name as model string

## Evidence
## Verification Gap

**Source:** epic-verify-p3p2j3nu.md, line 3 ("Default panel [claude,codex,gemini] runs end-to-end on Claude host with Stop-hook gating"); plan docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md lines 263-292 (roster schema example uses concrete models `claude-opus-4-7`, `gpt-5.5`, `gemini-3.1-pro`)
**Criterion AC-9:** "Default panel [claude,codex,gemini] runs end-to-end on Claude host with Stop-hook gating."

## Problem

`builtInDefaultSlots` populates each slot with `Provider == Model` (e.g., `{Provider: "claude", Model: "claude"}`), so the no-flag default path invokes `claude --model claude`, `codex --model codex`, `gemini --model gemini`. Whether the upstream CLIs accept the provider name as a model identifier cannot be confirmed in a read-only environment, and existing integration tests bypass the default path by passing `--agents claude,codex,gemini` explicitly.

## Search Performed

- `internal/roster/roster.go:15-19` — `builtInDefaultSlots = []RosterSlot{{Provider:"claude", Model:"claude"}, {Provider:"codex", Model:"codex"}, {Provider:"gemini", Model:"gemini"}}`
- `internal/reviewer/spawn.go:120-148` — `Runner.command` always emits `--model <slot.Model>` for all three providers
- `internal/cli/spawn_code_review_test.go:13-29` — `TestSpawnCodeReviewAgentsConsensusHappyPath` exercises only the `--agents` override path, not the no-flag built-in default
- Plan line 372 acknowledges: "The exact provider CLI flag names are subject to validation against the upstream CLIs in Phase B"

## Suggested Action

1. Either (a) replace the placeholder model strings in `internal/roster/roster.go:15-19` with concrete defaults that the CLIs accept (e.g., `claude-opus-4-7`, `gpt-5.5`, `gemini-3.1-pro` per plan example), or (b) add a Phase B integration test that exercises the no-flag default path against the mock CLIs to lock in whatever default contract is intended
2. If the placeholder strings are intentional (CLI auto-selects when given the alias), add a code comment in `roster.go` documenting the intent and the upstream CLI behavior verified

## Priority
P2 (informational)

## Resolution
This is advisory (P2/P3) and does not block epic closure. When complete, close this issue.

title: [T201] [integration-path-test] End-to-end single-pass review: spawn-code-review -> mock CLIs -> aggregate -> resolved gate -> Stop hook
description:
**Source Documents**:
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L160-L161](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L160-L161) — Section: High-Level Approach (Phase B goal: default panel works on Claude host with Stop-hook gating)

- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L94-L94](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L94-L94) — Spec §2 Key states: pending → resolved
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L766-L766](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L766-L766) — Section: Test Layers (integration: spawn → wait → resolve)
- Spec: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L93-L101](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L93-L101) — Spec §2 Key states (Empty/Pending/Resolved Stop-hook behavior)

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P1
**Story**: [Epic B]
**Parallel**: no (skeleton)
**Primary Files**: tests/integration/single_pass_e2e_test.go, internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go (skeleton), internal/state/state.go (skeleton)
**Subsystems**: tests/integration, internal/orchestrator, internal/state
**Dependencies**: none (this is the integration path test for Epic B)

**Goal**: Land an end-to-end Go integration test that runs `cerberus spawn-code-review` against an in-process reviewer subprocess stub, asserts (a) the gate transitions `pending → resolved`, (b) the aggregate verdict appears in `gate-state.json`, (c) the Stop hook poll loop returns success when status flips to resolved. This test is the skeleton + integration spine that all other Epic B tasks plug into.

**Context**: Phase B goal per plan §High-Level Approach: "default panel `[claude, codex, gemini]` works on Claude host with Stop-hook gating." This integration test fixes the contract between every Epic B subsystem (state, roster, reviewer, aggregate, orchestrator, hook) so each subsequent task can be implemented and tested incrementally against the same end-to-end shape. Per plan §Test Layers, "integration tests cover spawn → wait → resolve."

This task delivers the test scaffolding and minimal stubs in `internal/orchestrator` and `internal/state` so the test compiles. Real implementations land in T202–T207 and depend on T201.

**Scope**:
- In: `tests/integration/single_pass_e2e_test.go` orchestrating: a temp `<state_root>` dir, env wiring (CERBERUS_HOST=claude, CERBERUS_STATE_ROOT, CERBERUS_PROJECT_KEY, CERBERUS_RUN_KEY); injects a stub reviewer interface that returns a canned per-reviewer JSON (PASS verdicts, confidence 0.9); calls the orchestrator entry point; asserts `gate-state.json.status == "resolved"`, `verdict == "pass"`, and a Stop-hook helper returns 0 within a short timeout. Skeleton stubs in `internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go` and `internal/state/state.go` that compile but error out (`return errors.New("not implemented")`) — real bodies land in dependent tasks.
- Out: real reviewer subprocess (T204); real roster loader (T203); real aggregator beyond the trivial case (T205); telemetry JSON files beyond `gate-state.json` (T206); CLI subcommand wiring (T208); hook poll loop body (T207).

**Changes**:
- `tests/integration/single_pass_e2e_test.go` — [New] — Drives the end-to-end flow with an injected reviewer stub.
- `internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go` — [New, skeleton] — Defines `RunSinglePass(ctx, env, params, reviewer ReviewerSpawner)` signature; returns `errors.New("not implemented")` until T205/T206 fill it in.
- `internal/state/state.go` — [New, skeleton] — Defines `WriteGateState`, `ReadGateState`, `GateStatePending`, `GateStateResolved` constants/helpers; T206 fills bodies.
- `internal/reviewer/reviewer.go` — [New, interface only] — Defines `Spawner` interface so the test can inject a stub. Real implementation is T204.

**Wiring Map**: `test → orchestrator.RunSinglePass(env, params, stubReviewer) → internal/state.WriteGateState (pending) → stubReviewer.Spawn → aggregate.Compute → state.WriteGateState (resolved) → hook.PollGateState → assert resolved`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: Test compiles and is in skip-pending state (`t.Skip("pending T2xx implementations")`) until upstream tasks fill the stubs; once T202–T207 land the test passes against the real implementations and the Skip is removed.
- AC2: Test exercises the full path end-to-end (spawn → reviewer stub → aggregate → state write → poll → resolved) with no v1 fault-tolerance accretions; failures bubble up as Go test failures.

**Verification**:
- `go test ./tests/integration/single_pass_e2e_test.go` — initially the test runs but skips with the documented Skip reason; after dependent tasks land it passes without skip.

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate: this test must NOT exercise any v1 fault-tolerance accretion (JSON repair, fail-open, retry loops). On any error, the test fails fast.
- Per D46: when the test starts injecting real reviewer subprocesses (later tasks), the user prompt MUST be delivered via stdin, not argv. The Spawner interface should accept the prompt as an `io.Reader` or `[]byte` for stdin, not as a string in the command argv slice.
- Per simplification mandate: do NOT add advisory locking, retry-on-clobber, or graceful degradation to the test — those are explicit non-goals (D29).
- Do NOT touch run-team-related files (D9 cleanup is Epic F).
- The test is allowed to use `t.TempDir()` for `<state_root>` — no need for real `~/.claude/projects` paths.

## Unmet Criterion
[P1] AC-4 propagate roster mode/defaults into runtime

## Evidence
## Unmet Criterion

**Source:** docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md, line 261
**Criterion AC-4:** "Roster YAML schema closes D12/D15: version: 1, optional defaults(mode,max_rounds), required rosters map, required non-empty reviewers list, slot provider/model required, optional strategy/persona/mode, project roster precedence over user roster, CLI --reviewer append and --replace-slot semantics, <provider>#<index> instance IDs, and preflight rejection for unknown keys/providers/modes, missing strategy/persona, nonexistent replace slot, mutually exclusive --agents with --roster/--reviewer, missing default roster when no --roster, empty result, 1-reviewer debate panel, and unavailable CLI in custom rosters."

## Problem

Roster schema fields for `defaults.mode`, `defaults.max_rounds`, and per-slot `mode` are parsed and validated but not carried into the orchestrator path. This means the runtime does not honor part of the finalized D15 schema even when the YAML is valid.

## Evidence

- `internal/roster/types.go:19-23` — `RosterDefaults` defines `mode` and `max_rounds`, and `RosterSlot` defines per-slot `mode`.
- `internal/roster/preflight.go:93-103` — defaults are validated for known mode and positive max rounds.
- `internal/cli/spawn_code_review.go:179-188` — conversion from `roster.RosterSlot` to `orchestrator.ReviewerSlot` copies ID/provider/model/strategy/persona, but drops `Mode` and `InstanceIndex`.
- `internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go:70-77` — runtime mode and max rounds come only from `Params`, defaulting to `smart` and `1`; roster defaults are not consulted.
- Trace: `rosters.yaml` defaults/per-slot mode → `roster.ResolveWithOptions` validates fields → CLI drops fields during reviewer conversion → orchestrator uses CLI/default params instead of roster schema values

## Required Fix

1. Extend the resolved CLI/orchestrator parameter model to carry roster `defaults.mode`, `defaults.max_rounds`, and per-slot `mode` from `internal/roster` into `internal/orchestrator`.
2. Apply the plan's resolution order in `runSpawnCodeReview` before constructing `orchestrator.Params`, preserving CLI precedence where specified.

## Priority
P1 (blocking)

## Resolution
Address this criterion to unblock epic closure. When complete, close this issue.

[P1] AC-5 emit telemetry rows from production review path

## Evidence
## Unmet Criterion

**Source:** docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md, line 437
**Criterion AC-5:** "Telemetry JSON schema closes R8/D16: per-reviewer telemetry rows under iterations<N>/round-<R>/reviewers/<id>/telemetry.json include schema_version, reviewer_id=<provider>#<index>, instance_index, provider, model, strategy, persona_name, mode, tokens, cost_usd, peer_id, verdict, overall_confidence, round, time_to_finish_ms, started_at, ended_at; round telemetry and iteration telemetry are written under iterations<N>/ and aggregate totals include every slot exactly once."

## Problem

Telemetry schemas and writer functions exist, but the production single-pass path does not call the per-reviewer, round, or iteration telemetry writers. `RunSinglePass` writes only event-log entries and a run telemetry file without aggregating reviewer token/cost totals.

## Evidence

- `internal/telemetry/telemetry.go:20-38` — `ReviewerRow` defines the required per-reviewer telemetry fields.
- `internal/telemetry/telemetry.go:84-121` — writer functions exist for reviewer, round, and iteration telemetry paths.
- `internal/orchestrator/round.go:49-74` — round execution spawns reviewers and stores parsed outputs, but does not call `WriteReviewerRow` or collect token/cost/timing data.

title: [Review] 2 non-blocking findings from cerberus-6qt.8
description:
## Review Findings

This issue consolidates 2 non-blocking findings from code review.

**Source issue:** cerberus-6qt.8
**Highest priority:** P2

---

### Finding 1: [P2] Stop appending commit focus text as SHAs

**Priority:** P2
**Reviewer:** codex
**Location:** internal/cli/spawn_code_review.go:114-116

After any `--commit` is present, every remaining positional token is appended to `opts.commits`. A valid invocation such as `cerberus spawn-code-review --commit HEAD "focus on error handling"` therefore runs `git show ... HEAD "focus on error handling"` instead of putting the quoted text in `opts.focus`, causing the review to fail with an invalid revision. The parser needs to distinguish additional commit refs from trailing focus text rather than treating all `fs.Args()` as commits.

---

### Finding 2: [P2] Preserve existing git exclude pathspec magic

**Priority:** P2
**Reviewer:** codex
**Location:** internal/cli/spawn_code_review.go:292-294

`appendExcludes` unconditionally prefixes every user-supplied exclude with `:(exclude)`. If a caller passes an already valid git exclude pathspec such as `--exclude ':(exclude,glob)dist/**'`, it becomes `:(exclude):(exclude,glob)dist/**`, which no longer excludes the intended files. Since the option is documented as accepting pathspecs, existing magic forms like `:(exclude,glob)` and `:!` should be passed through or normalized without double-prefixing.

---

## Unmet Criterion
[P1] AC-6 emit the D16 telemetry lifecycle events

## Evidence
## Unmet Criterion

**Source:** epic-verify-u26w0eag.md, line 3
**Criterion AC-6:** "R8/D16 telemetry schema is implemented for Phase B: per-reviewer telemetry under iterations/<N>/round-<R>/reviewers/<id>/telemetry.json includes reviewer_id=<provider>#<index> and instance_index, with round/iteration/run telemetry and event log written by the single-pass runtime."

## Problem

The telemetry files and per-reviewer schema are implemented, but the D16 event-log contract is incomplete. The runtime emits `cerberus.reviewer.started` instead of the plan's `cerberus.reviewer.spawned`, does not emit `cerberus.roster.selected` on successful roster resolution, and does not emit `cerberus.preflight.failed` when CLI/roster preflight rejects before the run starts.

## Evidence

- `docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md:510` — D16 defines event-log names as mirroring the instrumentation event list, including `cerberus.roster.selected`, `cerberus.preflight.failed`, and `cerberus.reviewer.{spawned,completed,failed}`.
- `internal/telemetry/events.go:15-20` — event constants define `cerberus.roster.selected`, `cerberus.preflight.failed`, `cerberus.review.spawned`, and `cerberus.reviewer.started`, but not `cerberus.reviewer.spawned`.
- `internal/orchestrator/round.go:61-80` — reviewer launch emits `EventReviewerStarted`, so `event-log.jsonl` records `cerberus.reviewer.started` instead of the required `cerberus.reviewer.spawned`.
- `internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go:119-128` — the single-pass success path emits only `cerberus.review.spawned` at run start; no `cerberus.roster.selected` event is written.
- `internal/cli/spawn_code_review.go:33-48` — flag/roster preflight errors return before `RunSinglePass`, with no `cerberus.preflight.failed` event emission.
- Trace: `spawn-code-review` → `resolveReviewers`/preflight → `RunSinglePass` → event log misses/renames required D16 lifecycle events → telemetry consumer sees non-conforming event stream.

## Required Fix

1. Replace or alias the reviewer-start event in `internal/telemetry/events.go` and `internal/orchestrator/round.go` so the event log uses `cerberus.reviewer.spawned` per D16.
2. Emit `cerberus.roster.selected` after successful roster resolution and `cerberus.preflight.failed` for validation/preflight rejection paths, with enough run/root context for `event-log.jsonl` to be written consistently.

P1 (blocking)

title: [T202] internal/state: gate-state.json schema + read/write helpers (pending → resolved)
description:

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P1
**Story**: [Epic B]
**Parallel**: [P]
**Primary Files**: internal/state/state.go, internal/state/state_test.go, internal/state/paths.go
**Subsystems**: internal/state
**Dependencies**: T201

**Goal**: Implement `internal/state` per plan §State Tree Layout: GateState struct with the documented schema (schema_version, run_key, host, project_key, session_id, transcript_path, status, verdict, current_iteration, max_rounds, debate, roster_id, started_at, ended_at), read/write helpers, status transition `pending → resolved`, and on-disk path computation rules. This is the single source of truth for `gate-state.json` I/O per the R3 invariant lint.

**Context**: The gate-state.json schema is finalized at plan L409-L427. The state derivation rules (L429-L433) define `<state_root>`, `<run>`, and `<project_key>` in host-neutral terms — the actual host-specific `<state_root>` value comes from `internal/host` (T103, Epic A). Status transitions are the simplest possible: `pending → resolved`. v1's `awaiting_decision`/`requires_decision`/`error` intermediate states are explicitly NOT carried forward (plan L435 simplification mandate).

**Scope**:
- In: `internal/state.GateState` struct (matches plan L409-L427 JSON schema 1:1); `WriteGateState`, `ReadGateState`, `MarkResolved` helpers; per-reviewer `WriteReviewerOutput(runRoot, iteration, round, instanceID, jsonBytes)` writer; path-builder helpers for `<state_root>/<project>/<run>/iterations/<N>/round-<R>/reviewers/<instance_id>/`.
- Out: telemetry JSON files (T206); event-log.jsonl (T206); roster ID derivation (T203); session-id minting (lives in `internal/host`, T103).

**Changes**:
- `internal/state/state.go` — [New] — `GateState` struct + JSON tags matching plan §State Tree Layout; `WriteGateState(path string, gs *GateState) error`; `ReadGateState(path string) (*GateState, error)`; `MarkResolved(gs *GateState, verdict string, endedAt time.Time)`; `StatusPending`/`StatusResolved` consts.
- `internal/state/paths.go` — [New] — Path computation for run/iteration/round/reviewer dirs; `EnsureRunDir`, `IterationDir(runRoot, n)`, `RoundDir(...)`, `ReviewerDir(...)`. Uses `os.MkdirAll`.
- `internal/state/state_test.go` — [New] — Tests: GateState round-trips (write → read identical); MarkResolved sets status + verdict + ended_at; path helpers produce the exact spec-bound layout (`iterations/1/round-1/reviewers/codex#1/`).

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: GateState round-trips through `WriteGateState`/`ReadGateState` with byte-identical JSON keys per the schema in plan §State Tree Layout (schema_version, run_key, host, project_key, session_id, transcript_path, status, verdict, current_iteration, max_rounds, debate, roster_id, started_at, ended_at).
- AC2: `MarkResolved` transitions a GateState from `status: pending` to `status: resolved` with the supplied verdict and `ended_at` timestamp; the resulting JSON serializes verdict as one of `pass | fail | requires_decision` (no v1 intermediate states).

**Verification**:
- `go test ./internal/state/...`

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per plan L435 simplification mandate: do NOT support v1 intermediate states (`awaiting_decision`, `error`, etc.). Only `pending → resolved`.
- Per R3 invariant lint (plan L226 + §Module Layout note): this is the SINGLE source of truth for `gate-state.json` I/O. Other packages must call into `internal/state` and not write the file directly.
- Per D29: do NOT add advisory locks or atomic-rename. A second writer simply wins; a stderr warning is the orchestrator's job (T207).
- The schema_version field is set to `1` always at v2.0 GA — no migration logic.

title: [T203] internal/roster: YAML loader (KnownFields strict) + slot resolver + instance ID assignment + preflight validation
description:
**Source Documents**:

- Spec: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L134-L162](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L134-L162) — R2: roster config supports multi-instance + intra-provider model mixes

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P1
**Story**: [Epic B]
**Parallel**: [P]
**Primary Files**: internal/roster/roster.go, internal/roster/types.go, internal/roster/preflight.go, internal/roster/roster_test.go
**Subsystems**: internal/roster
**Dependencies**: T201, T202

**Goal**: Implement the roster YAML loader with strict-mode `KnownFields(true)`, the slot resolver (file precedence, CLI append with `--reviewer`, replace with `--replace-slot`), instance ID assignment (`<provider>#<index>` 1-based), built-in default panel `[claude, codex, gemini]`, and full preflight validation per plan §Roster YAML Schema.

**Context**: R2 + D15 specify the YAML schema (top-level `version: 1`, `defaults`, `rosters` map; per-slot `provider`, `model`, optional `strategy`, `persona`, `mode`). D19 mandates `yaml.v3` with `KnownFields(true)` so unknown keys at slot level cause preflight to reject. D45 sets the built-in default panel; D47 adds the rule that an existing rosters.yaml lacking a `default` roster errors instead of silently falling back. D33 emits a stderr warning for exact-duplicate slot tuples. D39/D13 distinguish built-in default (degrades on missing CLIs) from YAML rosters (reject on missing CLIs).

**Scope**:
- In: YAML schema struct types (Roster, RosterSlot per plan L232-L240); YAML loader using `yaml.v3` with strict KnownFields; resolution order per plan L302-L308 (file precedence ./.cerberus/ wins; built-in default if no file); CLI merge for `--reviewer` (append) and `--replace-slot`; instance ID assignment walking the resolved list with 1-based per-provider index; preflight validation for every failure case in plan L310-L324; stderr warnings per plan L325-L329.
- Out: per-CLI availability check (basic stub in this task using `exec.LookPath`; full fan-out and degraded-warning UX is wired in T207 orchestrator); the `--agents` legacy compatibility flag is acknowledged in preflight (mutually exclusive with `--roster`/`--reviewer`) but full surface lives at T208 CLI wiring; persona file content reading (T204).

**Changes**:
- `internal/roster/types.go` — [New] — `RosterSlot` struct per plan L232-L240; `Roster`, `RostersFile` parsing types matching the YAML schema.
- `internal/roster/roster.go` — [New] — `LoadRosters(path string) (*RostersFile, error)` using `yaml.v3` `KnownFields(true)`; `Resolve(file *RostersFile, name string, cliReviewers []string, replaceSlot string) ([]RosterSlot, error)` applying merge rules + instance-ID assignment.
- `internal/roster/preflight.go` — [New] — Validation: each preflight failure case in plan L310-L324 maps to a distinct error returning the file path, roster name, and slot index per R2 edge cases. Warnings per L325-L329 emitted to stderr.
- `internal/roster/roster_test.go` — [New] — Tests: (a) project rosters.yaml beats user; (b) D45 default panel when no file; (c) D47 error when file present but no `default` roster; (d) `--reviewer codex:gpt-5.5:verification-first` appends; (e) `--replace-slot codex#2 --reviewer codex:gpt-5.5:decompose` replaces; (f) duplicate `(provider, model, strategy)` triples both load and get distinct instance IDs `#1`, `#2` (and a stderr warning per D33); (g) unknown YAML key at slot level rejects with file path + slot index; (h) instance ID assignment walks the list 1-based per provider.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: A YAML file `version: 1` with a `default` roster `[claude, codex, gemini]` parses cleanly and assigns instance IDs `claude#1`, `codex#1`, `gemini#1`. A second `gemini` slot in the same roster gets `gemini#2`.
- AC2: Per D47, an existing rosters.yaml without a `default` roster and no `--roster` flag returns a preflight error whose message contains the file path, names both remediations (`pass --roster <name>` or remove the file), and includes the missing roster name.

**Verification**:
- `go test ./internal/roster/...`
- Manual: `bin/cerberus spawn-code-review` with no flags + no rosters.yaml uses built-in default; with rosters.yaml lacking `default` errors per D47.

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate: do NOT silently fall back when YAML is malformed; use loud preflight errors.
- Per D19: the YAML library is `gopkg.in/yaml.v3`. Use `decoder := yaml.NewDecoder(r); decoder.KnownFields(true)` for strict mode.
- Per D36: `--reviewer` grammar is `provider:model[:strategy]` only; persona and per-slot mode are YAML-only at v2.0. Reject if anything else appears in the colon-separated field.
- Per R2 edge cases: every preflight error MUST include file path + roster name + slot index in the message.
- Do NOT attempt D43 consensus mode parsing here; that lives in CLI flag wiring (T208) and aggregator (T205).

title: [T204] internal/prompts + internal/reviewer: subprocess runner with stdin user prompt (D46) + Gemini policy
description:
**Source Documents**:
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L102-L102](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L102-L102) — D46: Reviewer prompt delivered via stdin (NOT argv) to avoid E2BIG
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L202-L203](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L202-L203) — Section: Module Layout (`internal/prompts/`, `internal/reviewer/`)
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L357-L372](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L357-L372) — Section: Reviewer Subprocess Contract (compose, run, parse, write per slot; stdin user prompt for all 3 providers; Gemini policy file)
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L767-L767](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L767-L767) — Reviewer prompt size round-trip (256 KB stdin test)

- Spec: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L196-L210](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L196-L210) — R5: strategies + personas configurable per reviewer
- Spec: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L46-L46](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L46-L46) — Spec §1 Non-goal: per-reviewer JSON schema unchanged

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P1
**Story**: [Epic B]
**Parallel**: [P]
**Primary Files**: internal/prompts/compose.go, internal/prompts/compose_test.go, internal/reviewer/reviewer.go, internal/reviewer/spawn.go, internal/reviewer/parse.go, internal/reviewer/reviewer_test.go
**Subsystems**: internal/prompts, internal/reviewer
**Dependencies**: T201, T203

**Goal**: Implement (a) on-disk persona/strategy/reviewer-prompt composition (read at runtime per C4 — persona → strategy → reviewer prompt with `\n\n` separators), and (b) the reviewer subprocess runner that spawns the per-provider CLI (`claude`, `codex`, `gemini`), pipes the composed user prompt to the child via STDIN (D46, NOT argv), applies the Gemini read-only policy file for gemini slots (C5), strict-parses the per-reviewer JSON output, and writes per-reviewer outputs into the state tree.

**Context**: D46 is the binding rule: macOS `getconf ARG_MAX` is often ~256 KB which a code-review diff can blow past. Stdin is the uniform contract for all three providers; gemini falls back to `--prompt-file` only if Phase B confirms the installed CLI rejects stdin. The system prompt (small, infrequently multi-line) goes on argv via `--append-system-prompt`. Per-reviewer JSON schema does not change from v1: `findings[].confidence`, `overall_confidence`, `strategy`, `round`, `peer_responses_seen`, raw verdict in `PASS`/`FAIL`/`NEEDS_WORK` (D44 — normalization is the aggregator's job, T205).

**Scope**:
- In: `internal/prompts.Compose(slot, artifactType) ([]byte systemPrompt, []byte userPrompt, error)` reading persona file (if set), strategy file (if set, not `none`), reviewer prompt for the artifact type — concatenated `\n\n`; `internal/reviewer.Spawner` interface; concrete `Spawn(ctx, slot, system, user)` building the per-provider command per plan L364-L366 with user prompt via `cmd.Stdin`; Gemini path adds `--policy-file <CERBERUS_ROOT>/config/gemini-readonly-policy.toml` (C5); strict JSON unmarshal of stdout into the v1 per-reviewer schema; writes `prompt.md`, `output.json`, `stdout.log`, `stderr.log` under `iterations/<N>/round-<R>/reviewers/<instance_id>/` via `internal/state` helpers; large-prompt round-trip integration test (≥ 256 KB) per plan L767.
- Out: peer broadcast composition (debate, Epic C); per-reviewer telemetry row (T206); aggregator normalization (T205); CLI wiring (T208).

**Changes**:
- `internal/prompts/compose.go` — [New] — Compose persona + strategy + reviewer prompt; reads files at runtime (no embedding per D40).
- `internal/prompts/compose_test.go` — [New] — Tests: (a) persona+strategy+reviewer order with `\n\n` separators; (b) `strategy: none` suppresses strategy injection; (c) edited on-disk strategy file is picked up without rebuild (file mtime test).
- `internal/reviewer/reviewer.go` — [New] — `Spawner` interface (per T201 stub); `RawReviewerOutput` struct matching v1 per-reviewer JSON schema (verdict raw `PASS|FAIL|NEEDS_WORK`).
- `internal/reviewer/spawn.go` — [New] — `Spawn(ctx, slot, system, user) (*RawReviewerOutput, error)` builds per-provider `exec.CommandContext`; user prompt piped via `cmd.Stdin` (D46); system prompt via `--append-system-prompt <text>` argv flag; Gemini gets `--policy-file ${CERBERUS_ROOT}/config/gemini-readonly-policy.toml` (C5); writes stdout/stderr logs + prompt.md + output.json under reviewer dir; non-zero exit = reviewer failure (no retry); empty stdout = reviewer failure.
- `internal/reviewer/parse.go` — [New] — Strict `json.Unmarshal` into `RawReviewerOutput`; schema-parse errors are reviewer failures (no JSON repair per simplification mandate).
- `internal/reviewer/reviewer_test.go` — [New] — Unit tests with a mock provider binary stub: command construction (claude/codex/gemini); user prompt arrives on stdin (NOT argv); empty stdout fails; non-zero exit fails; Gemini policy-file flag present.
- `tests/integration/reviewer_largeprompt_test.go` — [New] — Composes a ≥ 256 KB user prompt and pipes it through to a mock CLI; asserts no E2BIG, sha256 round-trips intact, output JSON parses.

**Wiring Map**: `slot + artifact → prompts.Compose → (system, user) → reviewer.Spawn(cmd.Stdin = user, argv = [--append-system-prompt system, ...]) → exec → stdout JSON → parse → state.WriteReviewerOutput`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: For all three providers (claude, codex, gemini), the composed user prompt is delivered via `cmd.Stdin` (NOT argv); a unit test asserts the exec'd command's `Args` slice does NOT contain the user prompt body.
- AC2: When a `Gemini` slot is spawned, the command includes `--policy-file <CERBERUS_ROOT>/config/gemini-readonly-policy.toml`; a missing policy file produces a loud preflight-style error.

**Verification**:
- `go test ./internal/prompts/... ./internal/reviewer/...`
- `go test ./tests/integration/reviewer_largeprompt_test.go` — 256 KB prompt round-trip on darwin and linux.

**Notes for Agent**:
- D46 is BINDING: user prompt MUST be delivered via stdin. Reject any temptation to put it on argv (`-- <user>` or similar). System prompt stays on argv via `--append-system-prompt <text>`.
- Per D40: do NOT embed prompt files in the binary in v2.0 GA; on-disk read is mandatory. A missing `prompts/strategies/<name>.md` is a loud failure.
- Per D44: keep raw verdicts (`PASS`/`FAIL`/`NEEDS_WORK`) verbatim in `RawReviewerOutput`. Normalization to internal `pass`/`fail`/`requires_decision` is the aggregator's job (T205).
- Per simplification mandate: NO JSON output repair. Strict `json.Unmarshal`; failures propagate non-zero.
- Per simplification mandate: NO retry on subprocess failure; first non-zero exit propagates.
- The mock CLIs for tests live in `tests/mocks/{claude,codex,gemini}` per plan §Mock CLI Strategy — minimal stubs in this task; full fixture replay is Epic G.
- Gemini stdin contract: if Phase B confirms the installed gemini CLI rejects stdin, fall back to `--prompt-file <state_root>/.../prompt-stdin.md`. Pin a Decision-Log entry if needed.

title: [T205] internal/aggregate: confidence-weighted vote + verdict normalization (PASS/FAIL/NEEDS_WORK → pass/fail/requires_decision) + consensus modes
description:
**Source Documents**:
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L99-L100](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L99-L100) — D43 + D44: --consensus modes preserved; raw verdict normalization

- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L374-L385](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L374-L385) — Section: Aggregation (Compute(slots, outputs, mode); normalization; majority/all/any; blocking findings; failed subprocess fails gate)
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L763-L763](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L763-L763) — Section: Test Layers (aggregate: majority, all, any, blocking findings, raw verdict normalization)
- Spec: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L165-L174](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L165-L174) — R3: aggregation lives in one Go module shared by debate and non-debate paths

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P1
**Story**: [Epic B]
**Parallel**: [P]
**Primary Files**: internal/aggregate/aggregate.go, internal/aggregate/normalize.go, internal/aggregate/aggregate_test.go
**Subsystems**: internal/aggregate
**Dependencies**: T201, T204

**Goal**: Implement `internal/aggregate.Compute(slots, outputs, mode)` as the single source of truth for verdict computation: raw `PASS`/`FAIL`/`NEEDS_WORK` normalized to internal `pass`/`fail`/`requires_decision`; consensus modes `majority` (default) / `all` / `any` per D43; blocking findings prevent `pass`; any subprocess failure or schema-parse failure fails the gate (no fail-open).

**Context**: R3 mandates aggregation lives in one Go module shared by debate and non-debate paths; `internal/aggregate` is that module. Per R3 invariant lint design (plan L226), only `internal/aggregate` may DEFINE `Aggregate*` symbols; `internal/orchestrator` and `*_test.go` files are explicitly allowed to IMPORT them. Per D44, raw verdicts (`PASS`/`FAIL`/`NEEDS_WORK`) are preserved verbatim in telemetry; the gate-state schema uses normalized `pass`/`fail`/`requires_decision`. Per D43, three consensus modes preserve v1 surface.

**Scope**:
- In: `internal/aggregate.Mode` enum (`majority` default, `all`, `any`); `Compute(outputs []reviewer.RawReviewerOutput, mode Mode) (Result, error)` returning `{Verdict: pass|fail|requires_decision, Blockers []FindingRef}`; raw verdict normalization (`PASS`→`pass`, `FAIL`→`fail`, `NEEDS_WORK`→`requires_decision`); confidence-weighted vote per mode; blocking-severity findings prevent `pass` regardless of mode; any reviewer-output-parse failure surfaces here as a non-nil error (gate fails, no fail-open).
- Out: telemetry write of `blockers[]` (T206); event `cerberus.review.resolved` emission (T207 orchestrator); CLI flag parsing for `--consensus` (T208).

**Changes**:
- `internal/aggregate/aggregate.go` — [New] — `Mode` enum; `Result` struct; `Compute(outputs, mode) (Result, error)`; `majority`/`all`/`any` branches per D43.
- `internal/aggregate/normalize.go` — [New] — `NormalizeVerdict(raw string) (string, error)` mapping `PASS`→`pass`, `FAIL`→`fail`, `NEEDS_WORK`/equivalent→`requires_decision`; unknown raw verdict returns an error.
- `internal/aggregate/aggregate_test.go` — [New] — Tests: (a) `majority`: 2-of-3 PASS → pass; tie → requires_decision; (b) `all`: any non-PASS → fail; (c) `any`: at least one PASS → pass; (d) one reviewer with `severity: blocking` finding prevents `pass` regardless of mode; (e) raw verdict normalization (`PASS`→`pass`, `FAIL`→`fail`, `NEEDS_WORK`→`requires_decision`); (f) unknown raw verdict produces a loud error.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: `Compute(outputs, ModeMajority)` for the canonical 3-reviewer case `[PASS, PASS, FAIL]` returns `Result{Verdict: "pass"}`; for `[PASS, FAIL, NEEDS_WORK]` (no strict majority) returns `Result{Verdict: "requires_decision"}`.
- AC2: A reviewer with a `severity: blocking` finding causes the result to be `fail` or `requires_decision` (never `pass`) across all consensus modes; a unit test pins this.

**Verification**:
- `go test ./internal/aggregate/...`

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate (D44): preserve raw verdicts verbatim in the input (`PASS`/`FAIL`/`NEEDS_WORK`); normalization is internal-only and feeds the gate-state schema.
- Per simplification mandate: NO fail-open. A subprocess error or schema-parse failure surfaces here as a non-nil error from `Compute` and the gate fails.
- Per R3: this is the SINGLE source of truth. No `Aggregate*` symbols are defined elsewhere. The orchestrator imports this package and the R3 lint (Epic G) verifies the invariant.
- `Mode` should default to `majority` when unset (matches D43 default).
- Confidence-weighted: per plan §Aggregation L376, confidence-weighted means a PASS with confidence 0.9 outweighs a FAIL with confidence 0.4 — implement plainly without v1's complex tie-breakers.

title: [T207] internal/orchestrator + internal/hook: single-round runner + Stop hook poll loop + claude-session-start
description:
**Source Documents**:
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L99-L99](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L99-L99) — D38: internal MAX_WAIT_SECONDS = 1800; manifest timeout 2100
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L94-L94](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L94-L94) — D37: hook commands read payload from stdin (no $@)
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L172-L177](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L172-L177) — Section: Architecture (orchestrator instantiates a Run; hook poll loop)
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L204-L213](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L204-L213) — Section: Module Layout (`internal/orchestrator/`, `internal/hook/`)
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L94-L99](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L94-L99) — Spec §2 Key states (Pending: Stop hook polls every POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS up to MAX_WAIT_SECONDS)
- Spec: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L93-L101](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L93-L101) — Spec §2 Key states (Empty/Pending/Resolved + reviewer error = non-zero exit, no fail-open)

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P1
**Story**: [Epic B]
**Parallel**: no
**Primary Files**: internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go, internal/orchestrator/round.go, internal/hook/poll.go, internal/hook/claude.go, internal/orchestrator/orchestrator_test.go, internal/hook/poll_test.go
**Subsystems**: internal/orchestrator, internal/hook
**Dependencies**: T201, T202, T203, T204, T205, T206

**Goal**: Implement the single-round orchestrator (Run = preflight → spawn reviewers in parallel → aggregate → write gate-state.json + telemetry) and the Stop-hook poll loop (`hook claude-stop` reads payload from stdin per D37, polls `gate-state.json.status` every 3s up to internal `MAX_WAIT_SECONDS=1800` per D38). Includes `hook claude-session-start` minimal handler.

**Context**: Per plan §Architecture: `internal/orchestrator` instantiates a Run, fans out via `internal/reviewer` to one subprocess per slot, collects per-reviewer JSON, runs `internal/aggregate` for the verdict, and writes through `internal/state` and `internal/telemetry`. Per spec §2 Key states: Pending = Stop hook blocks and polls; Resolved = Stop hook allows. Per D37, hook payload comes via stdin (NOT `$@`). Per D38, internal MAX_WAIT_SECONDS=1800s gives a 5min buffer before the host's manifest 2100s hard-kill. Reviewer error = non-zero exit; no fail-open.

**Scope**:
- In: `internal/orchestrator.RunSinglePass(ctx, env, params, spawner)` doing preflight (calls into `internal/roster` resolution + CLI availability check w/ degraded panel + warning per D39 for built-in default) → writes `gate-state.json` (status: pending) → spawns reviewers in parallel via `internal/reviewer` → calls `internal/aggregate.Compute` → marks resolved → emits events via `internal/telemetry`. `internal/hook/poll.go` implements `PollGateState(path, pollInterval, maxWait)` — reads gate-state.json every 3s, returns nil when status is `resolved`, returns an error after MAX_WAIT_SECONDS. `internal/hook/claude.go` implements `HandleClaudeStop(stdinPayload, env)` and `HandleClaudeSessionStart(stdinPayload, env)`. D29 stderr warning when `gate-state.json` is already in `pending` state at spawn time.
- Out: codex-stop / codex-prompt-submit / codex-session-start (Epic E); debate multi-round (Epic C); peer broadcast (Epic C); the full CLI subcommand wiring is T208.

**Changes**:
- `internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go` — [New] — `RunSinglePass` entry; preflight pipeline including the D29 stderr warning for existing pending gate; emits `cerberus.review.spawned`, `cerberus.review.resolved` events.
- `internal/orchestrator/round.go` — [New] — `runRound(ctx, slots, spawner, prompts)` fans out goroutines (one per reviewer slot), collects results, returns aggregated outputs to the orchestrator. Per simplification mandate, NO retry on subprocess failure — first error fails the round.
- `internal/hook/poll.go` — [New] — `PollGateState(path, pollInterval=3s, maxWait=1800s)` poll loop; emits `cerberus.hook.blocked` / `cerberus.hook.allowed` events per spec §4.
- `internal/hook/claude.go` — [New] — `HandleClaudeStop(stdinPayload []byte, env *config.Env)` reads JSON payload from stdin (D37), resolves run root via `internal/host`, runs poll loop; `HandleClaudeSessionStart(stdinPayload []byte, env *config.Env)` initializes per-session state (transcript path + run key from payload).
- `internal/orchestrator/orchestrator_test.go` — [New] — Tests: gate transitions pending → resolved on success; reviewer subprocess failure fails the gate (non-zero error returned, no fail-open intermediate state); D29 warning emitted to stderr when starting on top of existing pending gate.
- `internal/hook/poll_test.go` — [New] — Tests: poll returns nil when gate-state.json status flips to resolved within max wait; poll returns error after max wait.

**Wiring Map**: `cli.HandleSpawnCodeReview → orchestrator.RunSinglePass → state.WriteGateState(pending) → round.runRound (fan-out reviewer.Spawn) → aggregate.Compute → state.MarkResolved → telemetry.WriteEvent(resolved)`; separately, `hook.claude-stop → poll.PollGateState → returns 0 when resolved, non-zero on max-wait timeout`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: With a stub spawner returning all-PASS reviewer outputs, `RunSinglePass` writes `gate-state.json` first with `status: pending`, then with `status: resolved` and `verdict: pass`; the Stop hook poll loop returns nil within 5 seconds.
- AC2: A reviewer subprocess that errors out causes `RunSinglePass` to return non-zero (no fail-open, no defensive `error` gate state); `gate-state.json` is not transitioned to `resolved`; the orchestrator's exit code propagates per simplification mandate.

**Verification**:
- `go test ./internal/orchestrator/... ./internal/hook/...`
- The Epic B integration test (T201) un-skips and passes against this implementation.

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate: NO retry, NO fail-open, NO mid-run defensive state. First error fails the gate and the orchestrator exits non-zero.
- Per D37: hook handlers read payload from `os.Stdin`. DO NOT depend on `os.Args` for hook payload data (positional `$@` forwarding is brittle through `sh -c`).
- Per D38: `MAX_WAIT_SECONDS = 1800s` internally (poll loop times out at 1800s); the manifest timeout 2100s is the host's responsibility (lives in `hooks/hooks.json` and is updated in Epic F).
- Per D29: emit a stderr warning when starting a spawn on top of an existing `pending` gate; do NOT lock or refuse.
- Do NOT touch `cerberus-task-completed-hook` or `cerberus-teammate-idle-hook` files — those are removed in Epic F.
- The `claude-session-start` handler initializes per-session run-key/transcript-path; no debate or run-team logic.

- `hooks/hooks.json:13-20` — Claude Stop hook invokes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/review-gate check` instead of `bin/cerberus hook claude-stop`.
- `internal/hook/claude.go:22-28` — `HandleClaudeStop` resolves the run and calls `PollGateState`, which is the Go blocking gate path.
- `internal/hook/poll.go:19-72` — `PollGateState` blocks while gate state is `pending` and returns only when resolved, missing, or timed out.
- `internal/cli/check.go:13-39` — Go `check` only prints `no active review` or the current status; it does not provide Stop-hook gating behavior.
- Trace: Claude Stop hook manifest → legacy `bin/review-gate check` → no Go `hook claude-stop` polling → expected Go Stop-hook gating path is bypassed

## Required Fix

1. Update `hooks/hooks.json` Stop command to lazy-build and execute `bin/cerberus hook claude-stop`.
2. Keep `internal/cli/check.go` as a status/check surface or explicitly route any hook-facing command through `hook.HandleClaudeStop`.

## Priority
P1 (blocking)

## Resolution
Address this criterion to unblock epic closure. When complete, close this issue.

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P1
**Story**: [Epic G]
**Parallel**: no (integration-path-test; foundation for other Epic G tasks)
**Primary Files**: tests/mocks/claude/main.go, tests/mocks/codex/main.go, tests/mocks/gemini/main.go, tests/fixtures/claude/, tests/fixtures/codex/, tests/fixtures/gemini/, tests/integration/mock_smoke_test.go
**Subsystems**: tests/mocks, tests/fixtures, tests/integration
**Dependencies**: T101 (skeleton), T104 (Makefile)

**Goal**: Land the three mock reviewer CLIs (claude/codex/gemini), a starter fixture set, and a smoke integration test that runs a mock against a fixture and verifies output. This is the integration path test for Epic G — every other Epic G task plugs into this scaffold.

**Context**: Per D22, each mock at `tests/mocks/{claude,codex,gemini}/main.go` is a tiny Go program that reads the user prompt from stdin (matching real CLIs per D46), computes `sha256(prompt)`, and replays the corresponding fixture JSON from `tests/fixtures/<provider>/<sha8>:<instance_id>.json`. Per D31, the fixture key includes `CERBERUS_MOCK_INSTANCE_ID` (passed via env by the test orchestrator). Missing fixtures fail loudly: the mock writes the prompt to `<key>.json.prompt.txt`, prints to stderr, and exits 2 (loud failure per simplification mandate).

The smoke integration test proves: (a) the mock binary builds via `go build`; (b) given a known fixture, invoking the mock with that prompt on stdin returns the fixture content on stdout exit 0; (c) given an unknown prompt, the mock writes the prompt-capture file and exits 2 with the expected stderr message.

**Scope**:
- In: `tests/mocks/claude/main.go`, `tests/mocks/codex/main.go`, `tests/mocks/gemini/main.go` (each ~40 LOC, identical shape per D22 sketch); a starter fixture set under `tests/fixtures/<provider>/` covering the happy-path verdict for each provider (1-2 fixtures per provider is enough to seed the smoke test); `tests/integration/mock_smoke_test.go` that builds + executes a mock and asserts both happy-path and missing-fixture behaviors.
- Out: integration tests that exercise the orchestrator end-to-end (T702); fixture set covering debate round 2 / multi-instance / persona-strategy injection (T702); CI workflow + lint targets (T703); binary-size assertion (T704); largeprompt round-trip (T705); fixtures-refresh implementation against real CLIs (T706).

**Changes**:
- `tests/mocks/claude/main.go` — [New] — Go program per D22 sketch: read stdin → sha256 → key with CERBERUS_MOCK_INSTANCE_ID → read `${CERBERUS_FIXTURE_DIR}/<sha8>:<instance_id>.json` → write to stdout. Missing fixture: capture prompt to `<key>.json.prompt.txt`, stderr error "mock-claude: no fixture for prompt+instance; wrote <path>", exit 2.
- `tests/mocks/codex/main.go` — [New] — Same shape, provider name = codex.
- `tests/mocks/gemini/main.go` — [New] — Same shape, provider name = gemini.
- `tests/fixtures/claude/<sha8>:<instance_id>.json` — [New] — At least one happy-path fixture (PASS verdict, valid per-reviewer JSON shape per D44). Same for codex/gemini.
- `tests/integration/mock_smoke_test.go` — [New] — Builds each mock via `go build`; for each provider, invokes the mock with the known fixture's prompt on stdin (CERBERUS_MOCK_INSTANCE_ID set) and asserts stdout == fixture bytes + exit 0; invokes with an unknown prompt and asserts exit 2 + capture file written + stderr matches.

**Wiring Map**: `prompt on stdin → mock binary → sha256(prompt) + instance_id → tests/fixtures/<provider>/<key>.json → stdout`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: Each mock binary builds via `go build ./tests/mocks/<provider>/` with no Cgo dependency.
- AC2: `go test ./tests/integration/ -run TestMockSmoke` passes — happy path replays the fixture; missing-fixture path exits 2 and writes the `.prompt.txt` capture file.
- AC3: The mock matches the contract assumed by `internal/reviewer` (Epic B): reads prompt from stdin per D46, accepts `CERBERUS_FIXTURE_DIR` + `CERBERUS_MOCK_INSTANCE_ID` env vars, writes JSON to stdout.

**Verification**:
- `go build ./tests/mocks/claude/ ./tests/mocks/codex/ ./tests/mocks/gemini/`
- `go test ./tests/integration/ -run TestMockSmoke`
- Manually invoke a mock with a known fixture's prompt: `echo "<prompt>" | CERBERUS_FIXTURE_DIR=tests/fixtures/claude CERBERUS_MOCK_INSTANCE_ID=claude#1 ./mock-claude`

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate (D22): missing fixtures fail loudly with exit 2 and a captured `.prompt.txt`. Do NOT add silent fallbacks, retries, or attempt to call real CLIs.
- Per D31: the key MUST include `instance_id` (`<sha8>:<instance_id>`). A keyed-by-prompt-only mock breaks debate's near-identical round-2 prompts.
- Per D46: the mock reads the prompt from `os.Stdin` only. Do not parse argv for prompts.
- Keep each mock under ~50 LOC. The shape is identical across providers — extract a tiny shared helper if you want (`tests/mocks/internal/replay/replay.go`) but only if it stays simple.
- Starter fixtures should be minimal (one happy-path PASS per provider). Extensive fixture coverage lives in T702 and is generated via `make fixtures-refresh` (T706).
- Do NOT write the actual integration tests for orchestrator/aggregate/anonymize end-to-end here — that is T702.
- Ensure the mocks compile with the same `-tags netgo` posture as the main binary (no Cgo).

title: [T703] .github/workflows/ci.yml full matrix + make lint structural checks
description:
**Source Documents**:
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L165-L165](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L165-L165) — Section: High-Level Approach (Phase G CI/tests goal)

- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L815-L821](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L815-L821) — Section: make lint enforces (zero-bash compound; no run-team refs; SKILL.md surface; manifest version; bootstrap drift detector)
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L226-L226](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L226-L226) — Section: Architecture (R3 lint: any .go file outside internal/aggregate, internal/anonymize, internal/state defining Aggregate*/Anonymize* or writing gate-state.json directly fails)
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L770-L771](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L770-L771) — Section: Structural lint + Regression list (zero bash/sh, no run-team refs, no review-gate refs)
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L820-L820](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L820-L820) — Plugin manifest versions: both at 2.0.0 at GA tag
- Spec: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L217-L231](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L217-L231) — R6: CI matrix (Claude × Codex × generic, darwin × linux); structural lint: zero bash/sh; no run-team refs

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P1
**Story**: [Epic G]
**Parallel**: [P]
**Primary Files**: .github/workflows/ci.yml, Makefile, scripts/lint/zero-bash.sh OR Go-based lint runner under internal/lint/
**Subsystems**: ci, build, lint
**Dependencies**: T701 (mocks must exist before lint can verify them), T702 (integration tests must exist before CI runs them)

**Goal**: Replace the Phase A skeleton workflow (T105) with the full CI matrix specified in plan §CI Matrix, and implement the `make lint` target body covering all five structural checks (zero-bash compound; no run-team refs; SKILL.md surface; R3 single-source-of-truth; plugin manifest versions; SKILL/hook bootstrap drift detector).

**Context**: Per spec R6, CI MUST run the v2 test suite against `CERBERUS_HOST=claude|codex|generic` on darwin and linux, blocking merge on regression. Per plan §CI Matrix, the canonical workflow has two jobs: `test` (os × host matrix; fail-fast: false) and `build-matrix` (os × arch cross-compile). `make lint` enforces the structural invariants that prevent v1 patterns from creeping back.

The five lint enforcement areas:
1. **Zero-bash compound** (plan L816-L817): allowlist `bin/` to ONLY contain `bin/cerberus`; reject any other tracked file under `bin/` (extension or no extension); reject any file under `bin/` whose first line begins with `#!` followed by `sh|bash|dash|zsh|env (sh|bash|dash|zsh)`. Note that `bin/cerberus` is gitignored per D32, so the tracked-files check effectively requires `bin/` to be empty in the repo at GA.
2. **No run-team refs** (plan L818): `grep -RIl 'task-completed-hook\|teammate-idle-hook' skills hooks agents bin` must be empty.
3. **SKILL.md surface** (plan L819): each surviving SKILL.md references `bin/cerberus` and NOT `bin/review-gate-models.sh` or `bin/review-gate`.
4. **Plugin manifest versions** (plan L820): `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` both advertise `2.0.0` at GA tag.
5. **R3 single-source-of-truth** (plan L226): any `.go` file outside `internal/aggregate`, `internal/anonymize`, `internal/state` defining top-level symbols matching `Aggregate*`/`Anonymize*` or writing `gate-state.json` directly fails the lint. Imports of these packages from `internal/orchestrator` and `*_test.go` are explicitly ALLOWED.
6. **Bootstrap drift detector** (plan L821): `prompts/host-neutral-bootstrap.md` shared resolver body matches the resolver region in each surviving SKILL.md and each hook `command` string. Per-caller `exec` lines are allowed to diverge.

The 256KB+ largeprompt test is run as part of the standard `make test` target on the matrix (it is implemented in T705); it is NOT a separate lint check. The binary-size assertion (D35) is wired in T704 within the build-matrix job.

**Scope**:
- In: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` rewrite per plan §CI Matrix; `make lint` target body implementing all six structural checks; helper scripts/Go programs as needed (kept under `internal/lint/` if Go-based; under `scripts/lint/` if bash — but per S3 / zero-bash mandate, prefer Go).
- Out: binary-size assertion (T704); 256KB+ largeprompt test code (T705); fixtures-refresh implementation (T706); integration test bodies (T702); mock CLIs (T701).

**Changes**:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — [Modify] — Rewrite to match plan §CI Matrix at L773-L813. Keep the matrix shape (`os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]`; `host: [claude, codex, generic]`; `fail-fast: false`); set `CERBERUS_HOST` env per matrix host; steps `make build && make test && make lint`; `build-matrix` job runs cross-compile for each (os, arch) combo (T704 adds the size assertion).
- `Makefile` — [Modify] — Replace the lint stub with the six structural checks. Implement zero-bash via Go (e.g., `go run ./internal/lint/zerobash`) so it stays portable; same for R3 SoT and bootstrap drift. Manifest version check is a one-liner via `jq` or Go-based JSON read. Surface checks use `grep -RIl` invocations that fail if the bad pattern matches.
- `internal/lint/zerobash/main.go` — [New] — Walks tracked files under `bin/` (via `git ls-files bin/` shelled out OR a stdlib walk against the working tree); fails if any file other than `bin/cerberus` is present, OR if any file under `bin/` starts with a shell shebang.
- `internal/lint/r3sot/main.go` — [New] — Walks `.go` files outside `internal/aggregate`, `internal/anonymize`, `internal/state`; uses `go/parser` to extract top-level decl names; fails on `Aggregate*`/`Anonymize*` matches or string-literal writes to `gate-state.json`. Allow `*_test.go` and `internal/orchestrator/` imports of these packages.
- `internal/lint/bootstrapdrift/main.go` — [New] — Reads `prompts/host-neutral-bootstrap.md`'s shared resolver body; checks every surviving `SKILL.md`'s bootstrap region and each `hooks/{hooks,codex-hooks}.json` `command` string contains the canonical body; per-caller `exec` lines allowed to diverge. Fails on mismatch with a diff line pinpointing the divergence.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: `make lint` passes against the v2 source tree at any phase past Phase F (Cleanup) and fails (with a clear error pinpointing the offender) when any of the six checks is violated. Verified by intentionally introducing each violation in a scratch branch.
- AC2: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` matrix runs `make build && make test && make lint` on every (os, host) combo and the build-matrix job runs cross-compile per plan §CI Matrix.
- AC3: A push event triggers all matrix cells; `fail-fast: false` is set so a single failure does not cancel the rest of the matrix (R6 verification: "every test in the matrix passes").

**Verification**:
- `make lint` locally on a clean v2 tree.
- Intentionally add a `bin/foo.sh` file → `make lint` fails with the zero-bash check error.
- Intentionally add a `AggregateX` symbol in `internal/orchestrator/` (outside the SoT packages) → R3 lint fails.
- Edit a SKILL.md to drop the canonical bootstrap body → drift detector fails.
- Push to a feature branch, observe matrix workflow runs each (os, host) combo.

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate: write the lint helpers in Go (`internal/lint/<check>/main.go`) rather than bash. This preserves the zero-bash mandate (S3) and keeps the binary surface portable.
- Per D17/D25 + plan §Lazy Build Trigger Notes (L626-L657): the bootstrap-drift detector compares ONLY the shared resolver body. Per-caller exec lines (`exec "\" "\"` for skills vs `exec "\" hook <name>` for hooks) are allowed to diverge.
- Per D32: `bin/cerberus` is gitignored. The zero-bash check runs against TRACKED files under `bin/` so an empty `bin/` directory passes.
- Per spec R10: both plugin manifests (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` AND `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`) must advertise `2.0.0` at GA. The lint check runs at every commit but the version is bumped to 2.0.0 in Epic F (the lint will fail if v2.0 GA tag is cut while a manifest is still at 1.x).
- Avoid introducing `actionlint` as a hard dependency; CI runs the workflow itself, which is the canonical validation.
- Do NOT add the binary-size assertion here — that is T704.
- Do NOT add the 256KB+ largeprompt test wiring here — that is T705.

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P2
**Story**: [Epic G]
**Parallel**: yes (parallel with T703 once T701 lands)
**Primary Files**: .github/workflows/ci.yml (modify — add the size-assertion step to the build-matrix job)
**Subsystems**: ci (1 subsystem)
**Dependencies**: T703 (full CI matrix wiring lands first)

**Goal**: Add the D35 binary-size assertion to the build-matrix job in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Per the canonical snippet in plan §CI Matrix L808-812, the assertion compares the produced binary size against 30 MB (darwin-arm64) or 35 MB (elsewhere) and fails the job if exceeded. Uses stat with the GNU/BSD fallback already shown in the plan snippet.

**Context**: Per spec R1 + D35, the binary size budget is a hard CI gate. v2 keeps the binary small via D18 (stdlib flag instead of cobra) + D19 (yaml.v3 only) + D40 (no embedded prompts). Adding the assertion in CI catches accidental dependency growth at PR time.

**Scope**:
- In: .github/workflows/ci.yml — add the size-assertion step to the build-matrix job per the plan §CI Matrix L808-812 snippet (verbatim shape: stat with GNU/BSD fallback, 30 MB cap on darwin-arm64, 35 MB elsewhere, fail with clear message naming the actual size + cap).
- Out: Local make-target equivalent (out of scope; CI is the gate); D35 cap renegotiation (a Decision-Log row if it ever fires).

**Changes**:
- .github/workflows/ci.yml — [Modify] — Add the binary-size assertion step to the build-matrix job after the go build step. Use the canonical snippet from plan L808-812 verbatim. Step name: 'Binary-size assertion (D35)'.

**Wiring Map**: build-matrix job → go build → size assertion step → fail-fast on cap exceedance. Surfaces in CI logs with the actual size + cap when violated.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: .github/workflows/ci.yml build-matrix job has a 'Binary-size assertion (D35)' step that runs after go build; the shell text matches plan §CI Matrix L808-812 (modulo whitespace).
- AC2: A deliberate test commit that bloats the binary above 30 MB on darwin-arm64 (e.g., embedding a large prompt blob) fails the build-matrix job with a clear stderr message naming the actual size + cap; reverting passes again.

**Verification**:
- grep -E 'D35|binary size|Binary-size' .github/workflows/ci.yml returns matches in the build-matrix section.
- A scratch branch with a deliberate bloater fails CI on the size step; reverting passes.

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate: do NOT add a 'best-effort' or 'warn' tier; D35 is a hard fail.
- Per D18/D19/D40: the existing dependency posture should sit comfortably under 30 MB on darwin-arm64; if T704's first run fires, treat as a real signal and investigate before bumping the cap.

title: [T705] tests/integration/reviewer_largeprompt_test.go (D46: 256KB+ stdin round-trip)
description:

- Spec: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L29-L29](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-spec.md#L29-L29) — Simplification mandate (loud failure on E2BIG would be unacceptable; stdin path required)

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P2
**Story**: [Epic G]
**Parallel**: yes (parallel with T702/T703/T704 once T701 lands)
**Primary Files**: tests/integration/reviewer_largeprompt_test.go (new)
**Subsystems**: tests/integration (1 subsystem)
**Dependencies**: T204 (internal/reviewer subprocess runner with stdin user prompt — D46 plumbing exists), T702 (full integration suite skeleton), T701 (mocks/fixtures available)

**Goal**: Author tests/integration/reviewer_largeprompt_test.go enforcing D46: a ≥ 256 KB user prompt is delivered to the reviewer subprocess via stdin (NOT argv) and round-trips intact. Test runs across the OS × host CI matrix on darwin and linux. Asserts no exec.E2BIG, the mock receives the full prompt on stdin, and the prompt's sha256 round-trips intact through to the canonical reviewer output JSON.

**Context**: Per D46, code-review prompts (artifact diff + author-context + debate peer broadcast) routinely exceed macOS getconf ARG_MAX (~256 KB). v1 invocation embedded prompt on argv and would have hit E2BIG at scale. v2 wires user prompts through stdin (D46) and OS-level fall-back to a temporary prompt-stdin.md file via --prompt-file for any provider that rejects stdin (Phase B verifies, especially gemini).

**Scope**:
- In: tests/integration/reviewer_largeprompt_test.go — composes a ≥ 256 KB user prompt; spawns the reviewer subprocess via internal/reviewer; asserts (a) no E2BIG / argument list too long error from exec, (b) the mock CLI received the full prompt on stdin (sha256 round-trip via the mock writing the received prompt back into stats), (c) the canonical reviewer output JSON parses cleanly.
- Out: Generator large-prompt round-trip (T404 / T405 cover the generate path); fall-back to --prompt-file (Phase B Decision-Log row if a real provider rejects stdin — not test scope).

**Changes**:
- tests/integration/reviewer_largeprompt_test.go — [New] — Build a 256 KB+ random user prompt; call internal/reviewer.Spawn with the test mock CLI; assert no E2BIG (test fails if exec returns the syscall error); the mock writes its received-prompt sha256 to stats.json; the test asserts the round-trip sha matches.

**Wiring Map**: tests/integration/reviewer_largeprompt_test.go → internal/reviewer.Spawn → tests/mocks/<provider>/main.go (reads stdin, returns fixture + reflects sha256) → fixture JSON. Runs in CI on (ubuntu-latest, macos-latest) × (claude, codex, gemini) — at least one mock per provider since D46 says all three accept stdin.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: tests/integration/reviewer_largeprompt_test.go passes on darwin and linux: no E2BIG, the mock-received prompt sha256 matches the input prompt's sha256, the reviewer output JSON parses.
- AC2: Test exercises all three providers (claude, codex, gemini) — at least one parameterized subtest per provider mock; failure messages clearly state which provider failed and at which step (exec / stdin read / JSON parse).
- AC3: A deliberate test commit that reverts internal/reviewer to argv-mode (e.g., calls cmd.Args = append(cmd.Args, prompt) instead of cmd.Stdin) fails this test on darwin with E2BIG within seconds; reverting passes.

**Verification**:
- go test -run TestReviewerLargePromptStdinRoundTrip ./tests/integration/ → passes on darwin and linux.
- A scratch branch with argv-mode regression fails the test on darwin within 5 seconds (E2BIG path).

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate: failure on E2BIG is a real fault — do NOT make the test best-effort. It must hard-fail on E2BIG.
- Per D46: the fall-back path (--prompt-file for gemini if stdin rejects) is a Phase B finding, not part of this test's happy path.
- Test should not require real provider CLIs; uses mock CLIs from T701.

description:

**Primary Files**: Makefile (modify — add fixtures-refresh target)
**Subsystems**: build (1 subsystem)
**Dependencies**: T701 (mocks + fixtures layout exists)

**Goal**: Implement the make fixtures-refresh target per D22 + OQ-Plan-2: a manual maintainer operation that runs real claude / codex / gemini CLIs against a known set of test prompts and writes/overwrites the frozen fixture JSON files in tests/fixtures/<provider>/<sha8>:<instance_id>.json. Not part of CI.

**Context**: Per D22, the mock CLI strategy keys fixtures on sha256(prompt) + ':' + instance_id. When a reviewer prompt template changes (or a real CLI updates), the hash changes and tests fail loudly with the prompt written to disk. The maintainer runs make fixtures-refresh to regenerate. Per OQ-Plan-2, this manual loop is sufficient for v2.0; deeper automation is v2.x.

**Scope**:
- In: Makefile fixtures-refresh target that (a) requires real claude/codex/gemini on PATH, (b) iterates a curated list of test prompts (committed under tests/fixtures/_prompts/ as plain text), (c) invokes each real CLI with the appropriate flags from internal/reviewer's contract, (d) hashes each prompt + instance_id, (e) writes the canonical reviewer output JSON to tests/fixtures/<provider>/<key>.json. Surfaces missing-CLI errors loudly per simplification mandate.
- Out: CI integration (D22 explicit: not part of CI); automated drift detection (OQ-Plan-2 v2.x candidate); fixture content hand-editing (out of scope; fixtures are CLI output).

**Changes**:
- Makefile — [Modify] — Add fixtures-refresh target. Calls a small helper (inline shell or a tiny Go tool under tests/fixtures/refresh.go) that walks tests/fixtures/_prompts/ and runs each real CLI against each prompt. Loud-fails if a CLI is missing.

**Wiring Map**: maintainer runs make fixtures-refresh → real CLIs spawn → outputs hashed by (sha8(prompt), instance_id) → tests/fixtures/<provider>/<key>.json overwritten. Mock CLIs (T701) read these fixtures during make test.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: make fixtures-refresh runs end-to-end on a maintainer box with real CLIs installed; produces (or overwrites) at least one fixture per provider under tests/fixtures/<provider>/; missing-CLI cases fail loudly with a single-line stderr message naming the missing CLI.
- AC2: The keying scheme matches T701's mock contract exactly: <sha8(prompt)>:<instance_id>.json under tests/fixtures/<provider>/; a unit-style smoke check inside the target verifies the keys match the mocks' lookup format.

**Verification**:
- make fixtures-refresh on a maintainer box with all three CLIs → produces fixtures; exit 0.
- make fixtures-refresh with one CLI missing → exits non-zero, single stderr line names the missing CLI.
- ls tests/fixtures/<provider>/<sha8>:<instance_id>.json after a refresh shows files in the expected layout.

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per D22: this target is maintainer-side and NOT run in CI.
- Per simplification mandate: missing-CLI is a loud failure, not a warn-and-skip.
- Per OQ-Plan-2: a 'fixtures-stale-check' is v2.x; do not add it here.
- Keep the prompt list under tests/fixtures/_prompts/ minimal — one prompt per surviving artifact type.

title: [Review] 1 non-blocking finding from cerberus-b31.8
description:
## Review Findings

This issue consolidates 1 non-blocking finding from code review.

**Source issue:** cerberus-b31.8
**Highest priority:** P2

---

### Finding 1: [P2] Unwrap parenthesized string expressions

**Priority:** P2
**Reviewer:** codex
**Location:** internal/lint/r3sot/main.go:121-122

`stringExprValue` only folds `BasicLit` and `BinaryExpr`, so a direct write like `os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(runRoot, ("gate-state"+".json")), data, 0o644)` reaches this default case as an `*ast.ParenExpr` and returns `ok=false`. That leaves a trivial composed `gate-state.json` write outside `internal/state` undetected even though the new lint is intended to catch these direct composed filenames.

description:

**Type**: task

**Story**: [Epic E]
**Parallel**: no (integration-path-test for Epic E)
**Primary Files**: internal/hook/codex.go, internal/hook/codex_test.go, internal/cli/hook.go, tests/integration/codex_hook_skeleton_test.go, tests/fixtures/codex/hook-payload-session-start.json, tests/fixtures/codex/hook-payload-prompt-submit.json, tests/fixtures/codex/hook-payload-stop.json
**Subsystems**: internal/hook, internal/cli, tests/integration
**Dependencies**: depends on Epic A (internal/cli dispatcher, internal/host) and Epic B (internal/hook claude-stop poll loop machinery)

**Goal**: Land the integration-path-test for Phase E: a thin skeleton for the three Codex hook handlers (codex-session-start, codex-prompt-submit, codex-stop) wired into internal/cli dispatch, plus an end-to-end integration test that pipes a mock Codex hook payload to each subcommand on stdin (per D37) and asserts the dispatch reaches Go code with the expected payload shape. This unblocks subsequent Epic E tasks (host adapter extension, real handler bodies, default-roster degradation) by proving the wiring works.

**Context**: Phase E delivers Codex first-class host parity per R4. Three new hook entry points are needed: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop. Per D37, hook payload is read from os.Stdin (not argv); sh -c '' forwarding is brittle. Per OQ-Plan-3, the Codex hook payload contract must be validated against the installed Codex CLI in Phase E — this task captures the assumed shape in test fixtures and surfaces deviation early. The integration-path-test pattern matches T101 / Epic B integration-path-test: minimal handlers (e.g. echo a synthetic event log line and exit 0) wired through the real cli.Run dispatch, exercised end-to-end by an integration test.

**Scope**:
- In: skeleton handler functions for codex-session-start / codex-prompt-submit / codex-stop in internal/hook/codex.go (each reads stdin, parses an assumed Codex payload shape, emits a single cerberus.hook.{allowed,blocked} event, exits 0); cli.Run wiring under hook subcommand dispatch; mock payload fixtures under tests/fixtures/codex/; integration test that builds the binary, pipes each fixture to stdin, asserts exit 0 and event-log line written.
- Out: Codex host adapter state-root resolution (T502); real session-state initialization (T503); real Stop poll loop (T504); default-roster degradation on Codex (T505); SKILL.md / hooks.json rewrites (Epic F).

**Changes**:
- internal/hook/codex.go — [New] — Three handler functions: HandleCodexSessionStart, HandleCodexPromptSubmit, HandleCodexStop. Each reads os.Stdin, json.Unmarshal into a CodexHookPayload struct (session_id, transcript_path, project_key, event-specific fields), emits a stub event, exits 0. Stop handler stubs the poll loop (returns immediately for skeleton; real loop in T504).
- internal/hook/codex_test.go — [New] — Unit tests: each handler accepts a fixture payload on stdin and emits the expected event; malformed JSON exits non-zero with a stderr message.
- internal/cli/hook.go — [Modify] — Extend the hook subcommand switch to dispatch codex-session-start / codex-prompt-submit / codex-stop to the new handlers (alongside the existing claude-* entries from Epic B).
- tests/integration/codex_hook_skeleton_test.go — [New] — Builds cmd/cerberus, invokes ./cerberus hook codex-session-start (and codex-prompt-submit, codex-stop) with each fixture piped to stdin, asserts exit 0 and event-log output.
- tests/fixtures/codex/hook-payload-{session-start,prompt-submit,stop}.json — [New] — Captured/synthesized Codex hook payload shapes (assumed contract per OQ-Plan-3; updated by T503/T504 if real-CLI smoke reveals deviation).

**Wiring Map**: stdin (Codex host JSON) → cmd/cerberus → internal/cli.Run → switch hook → switch codex-* → internal/hook.HandleCodex* → internal/telemetry event log

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: cerberus hook codex-session-start, cerberus hook codex-prompt-submit, cerberus hook codex-stop each accept a fixture payload on stdin (per D37), exit 0, and emit one cerberus.hook.allowed (or .blocked) event to the event log.
- AC2: tests/integration/codex_hook_skeleton_test.go builds the binary and exercises all three subcommands via stdin piping; passes on darwin and linux.
- AC3: Malformed JSON on stdin exits non-zero with a single-line stderr message naming the field that failed parse (no JSON repair per simplification mandate).

**Verification**:
- go test ./internal/hook/... ./tests/integration/...
- Manual: cat tests/fixtures/codex/hook-payload-session-start.json | ./bin/cerberus hook codex-session-start; assert exit 0.
- Schema check: payload struct fields match the assumed Codex contract (session_id, transcript_path, project_key, event-specific). T503/T504 update if Phase E smoke reveals deviation; OQ-Plan-3 closes when this happens.

**Notes for Agent**:
- This is the integration-path-test for Epic E. Keep handlers minimal — just enough to prove dispatch + stdin parse work. Real session-state / poll-loop / default-roster-degradation logic land in T503 / T504 / T505.
- Per simplification mandate: no fail-open hooks, no JSON repair, no env-var aliases. Fail loudly on malformed payload.
- Per D37: read os.Stdin directly; do NOT rely on \$@ forwarding through sh -c.
- Per R3 / D14: do NOT define gate-state writes outside internal/state, do NOT define aggregate/anonymize symbols outside their packages. Hook handlers compose existing internal packages but introduce no duplicates.
- Do NOT touch run-team / TaskCompleted / TeammateIdle wiring — D6/D9 is pure removal in Epic F.

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P1
**Story**: [Epic E]
**Parallel**: yes (parallel with T503/T504; both consume the host adapter)
**Primary Files**: internal/host/codex.go, internal/host/codex_test.go, internal/host/host.go (modify factory), tests/integration/codex_host_resolution_test.go
**Subsystems**: internal/host
**Dependencies**: T501 (Codex hook skeleton wired) and Epic A T103 (host adapter for claude/generic)

**Goal**: Add a Codex host adapter to internal/host that resolves CERBERUS_HOST=codex into the host-specific state root (~/.codex/projects/<project_key>/cerberus/), derives session_id and transcript_path from the Codex hook payload (per D37 stdin contract), and stamps gate-state.json.host=codex. Codex becomes a peer host (R4) — same state-tree shape, different root. Closes part of OQ-Plan-3 by pinning the assumed root env behavior.

**Context**: Per plan §State derivation rules, <state_root> defaults to ~/.claude/projects/<project_key>/cerberus/ for Claude host; Codex resolves an equivalent under ~/.codex/projects/<project_key>/cerberus/. Project key is sha256(absolute repo path)[0:16] for stability. <run> is the host-provided session_id. The host adapter is the seam between host-aware naming and host-neutral state tree shape — this is what makes Codex a peer host rather than an adapter (plan §Architecture).

**Scope**:
- In: NewCodexHost() factory branch in internal/host/host.go; codex.go implementing the same host adapter interface as claude.go (StateRoot, ProjectKey, ResolveSessionID(payload), TranscriptPath(payload)); unit tests for each method; an integration test that sets CERBERUS_HOST=codex, runs the gate-state writer, asserts gate-state.json lands under ~/.codex/.../cerberus/ and gate-state.json.host=="codex".
- Out: Hook handler bodies (T503/T504); default-roster degradation (T505); generic host adapter (already in T103).

**Changes**:
- internal/host/codex.go — [New] — CodexHost struct + methods. StateRoot returns filepath.Join(home, .codex, projects, projectKey, cerberus). ResolveSessionID/TranscriptPath read payload fields per the assumed Codex contract (validated against installed Codex CLI in T503/T504; deviation pinned via Decision-Log row).
- internal/host/host.go — [Modify] — Extend the factory: when CERBERUS_HOST=codex, return CodexHost{}. Default detection (CERBERUS_HOST unset) prefers existing claude detection logic.
- internal/host/codex_test.go — [New] — Unit tests: state root path computation, project-key sha256 derivation, session-id resolution from a fixture payload, transcript-path absolute-vs-empty handling.
- tests/integration/codex_host_resolution_test.go — [New] — Sets CERBERUS_HOST=codex + a temp HOME, exercises a stub spawn that writes gate-state.json, asserts the file lands under tmpHOME/.codex/projects/<key>/cerberus/<run>/gate-state.json and host==codex.

**Wiring Map**: env CERBERUS_HOST=codex → internal/host.New() → CodexHost{} → ResolveSessionID/StateRoot consumed by internal/state writers + internal/hook handlers

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: With CERBERUS_HOST=codex set, internal/host.New() returns a CodexHost whose StateRoot resolves to <HOME>/.codex/projects/<sha256(repo path)[0:16]>/cerberus/.
- AC2: gate-state.json written under the Codex state root has host="codex" and matches the host-neutral schema (plan §State Tree Layout).
- AC3: Unit tests cover state-root, project-key, session-id, and transcript-path derivation; failure cases (empty payload field) return a clear error rather than silently using empty strings.

**Verification**:
- go test ./internal/host/... ./tests/integration/codex_host_resolution_test.go
- Manual: env CERBERUS_HOST=codex HOME=/tmp/cerberus-test ./bin/cerberus hook codex-session-start < tests/fixtures/codex/hook-payload-session-start.json; assert state-root path.
- Confirm sha256(absolute repo path)[0:16] matches between Claude and Codex hosts so the same repo gets the same project key cross-host (per state-tree shape host-neutral invariant).

Per plan §Architecture, hook handlers are invoked after the same *config.Env resolution as other subcommands. Per D37, payload arrives on os.Stdin.

- AC1: Both codex-session-start and codex-prompt-submit handlers parse the assumed payload, write a session-state cache under the Codex state root (T502), emit a cerberus.hook.allowed event, and exit 0.
- AC2: A subsequent cerberus status invocation within the same session resolves session_id and transcript_path from the cache without re-reading the payload (proves the seed worked).

title: [T504] internal/hook: implement codex-stop handler (poll loop sharing claude-stop machinery; gate-state polling, MAX_WAIT_SECONDS=1800, manifest timeout 2100)
description:
