title: [T402] internal/generate orchestrator: parallel fan-out to claude/codex/gemini via internal/reviewer subprocess pattern + stdin user prompt (D46)
description:
**Source Documents**:
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L102-L102](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L102-L102) — D46: Reviewer prompt delivered via stdin (not argv) to avoid `E2BIG`; applies to all subprocess invocations.
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L357-L373](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L357-L373) — Section: Reviewer Subprocess Contract — per-provider invocation, system prompt on argv, user prompt via stdin, fail-loud on subprocess error.
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L181-L226](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L181-L226) — Section: Module/Package Layout — `internal/generate/` (multi-model draft generator).
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L162-L162](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L162-L162) — Phase D goal: `cerberus generate` subcommand for create-spec / create-plan / architecture-review / healthcheck multi-model drafts.
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L767-L767](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L767-L767) — Test layer: 256 KB+ prompt round-trip (D46) — applies to generators too since prompt files can be large.

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P2
**Story**: [Epic D]
**Parallel**: yes (with T403, T404)
**Primary Files**: internal/generate/generate.go, internal/generate/subprocess.go, internal/generate/subprocess_test.go, internal/generate/generate_test.go, internal/prompts/generators.go, internal/prompts/generators_test.go
**Subsystems**: internal/generate, internal/prompts
**Dependencies**: T401

**Goal**: Replace T401's serial skeleton with the production fan-out: parallel subprocess execution across `[claude, codex, gemini]` (one goroutine per provider, joined via `sync.WaitGroup` or `errgroup`); each goroutine reuses the subprocess helper that backs `internal/reviewer.Spawn` from Epic B (stdin user prompt per D46, system prompt on argv via `--append-system-prompt`, captured stdout, captured stderr); the generator system prompt is composed by `internal/prompts.ComposeGenerator(provider, type)` reading the on-disk template at `prompts/generators/<type>/<provider>.md` (existing v1 templates preserved per C4); per-provider stdout is written verbatim to `<output_dir>/<provider>/draft.md`; subprocess errors are surfaced loudly via the returned error (T403 refines to per-provider `.failed` markers + non-blocking).

**Context**: Per plan §Reviewer Subprocess Contract, the per-provider invocation pattern for `claude`/`codex`/`gemini` is well-defined: stdin = user prompt (D46 — avoids `E2BIG` on large prompts), argv contains `--append-system-prompt <system>` for claude, `--json --model <model> --append-system-prompt` for codex, `--json --model <model> --append-system-prompt --policy-file ${CERBERUS_ROOT}/config/gemini-readonly-policy.toml` for gemini. The generator path uses the same pattern but with generator-flavored prompt templates instead of reviewer prompts. Existing v1 templates live under `prompts/generators/<type>/{claude,codex,gemini}.md` (or equivalent — verify in repo); these are read at runtime per C4 (no embedding fallback per D40). Parallel execution matches v1 behavior (v1 fans out via `&` + `wait`); v2 uses goroutines + `errgroup`. Per simplification mandate, no JSON repair, no fail-open. C5 Gemini policy applies to every Gemini child including in generator runs (the `--policy-file` flag is still passed to the gemini subprocess); the v1 generator already enforces this and v2 must too.

**Scope**:
- In: `internal/generate/subprocess.go` defining a private `runProvider(ctx, provider, model, systemPrompt, userPrompt) (stdout []byte, stderr []byte, err error)` helper that calls the same subprocess plumbing as Epic B's `internal/reviewer.Spawn` — composes the per-provider argv (with `--policy-file` for gemini), pipes the user prompt to stdin, captures stdout/stderr, applies the orchestrator's deadline. Reuse via private helper or shared internal interface; do NOT duplicate the reviewer subprocess logic across packages (architectural cleanliness, not R3 — R3 is specifically about aggregate/anonymize/state).
- In: `internal/generate/generate.go` orchestrator: parallel fan-out via `errgroup.Group` over `[claude, codex, gemini]`; each goroutine calls `runProvider`, writes stdout to `<output_dir>/<provider>/draft.md`. The function returns the joined error (any provider error fails the whole Run; T403 will refine to per-provider isolation).
- In: `internal/prompts.ComposeGenerator(provider, generatorType string) (systemPrompt string, err error)` reads on-disk template at `prompts/generators/<generatorType>/<provider>.md`; returns error if file missing (loud failure per simplification mandate).
- In: tests covering: (a) parallel fan-out completes faster than 3x serial (mock CLIs each sleep 100ms; parallel total <200ms; serial >300ms); (b) per-provider stdout is written verbatim (no munging); (c) `ComposeGenerator` reads from disk at every call (no caching — C4); (d) gemini subprocess receives `--policy-file` in its argv (C5).
- Out: per-provider `<provider>.failed` markers + non-blocking failure semantics (T403); `raw.json` + `stats.json` outputs (T403); CLI flag surface (T404); per-`--type` integration coverage (T405).

**Changes**:
- `internal/generate/subprocess.go` — [New] — `runProvider(ctx, provider, model, systemPrompt, userPrompt)` private helper. For provider == claude: argv `[\"claude\", \"--print\", \"--output-format\", \"json\", \"--append-system-prompt\", systemPrompt]`. For codex: `[\"codex\", \"--json\", \"--model\", model, \"--append-system-prompt\", systemPrompt]`. For gemini: `[\"gemini\", \"--json\", \"--model\", model, \"--append-system-prompt\", systemPrompt, \"--policy-file\", policyPath]`. `cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(userPrompt)`. Returns stdout/stderr/err.
- `internal/generate/generate.go` — [Modify, replaces T401 skeleton] — `Run` uses `errgroup.Group` to fan out across providers in parallel; each goroutine: composes system prompt via `internal/prompts.ComposeGenerator`, calls `runProvider`, writes `<output_dir>/<provider>/draft.md`. Joined error returned.
- `internal/prompts/generators.go` — [New] — `ComposeGenerator(provider, generatorType string) (string, error)`; reads from `${CERBERUS_ROOT}/prompts/generators/<generatorType>/<provider>.md`; mode parameter (fast/smart/max) is folded into the system prompt or selected via a sub-template (verify in repo) — preserve v1 semantics.
- `internal/generate/subprocess_test.go` — [New] — Tests: argv composition for each provider; gemini argv includes `--policy-file`; user prompt reaches stdin (assert via mock that captures stdin and writes it to a check file).
- `internal/prompts/generators_test.go` — [New] — Tests: read from disk every call (modify file between calls, second read sees the new content); missing template returns error.
- `internal/generate/generate_test.go` — [Modify, replaces T401 skeleton] — Tests: parallel fan-out timing; per-provider stdout written verbatim; subprocess error surfaces from `Run`.

**Wiring Map**: `internal/cli/generate.go (T401) → internal/generate.Run(ctx, opts) → errgroup.Go × 3: internal/prompts.ComposeGenerator → runProvider (subprocess via Epic B reviewer pattern; user prompt via stdin per D46) → write <output_dir>/<provider>/draft.md`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: Fan-out is parallel: with three mock CLIs each sleeping 100ms, `Run` completes in <200ms (asserts `time.Since(start)` < 200ms in test).
- AC2: Gemini subprocess argv contains `--policy-file <CERBERUS_ROOT>/config/gemini-readonly-policy.toml` (C5 enforcement; assert via mock argv-capture stderr).
- AC3: User prompt reaches subprocess stdin (D46): a 256 KB user prompt round-trips intact (sha256 of stdin bytes received by mock matches sha256 of input prompt) — this exercises the same E2BIG-resistant path Epic B verifies for reviewers.

**Verification**:
- `go test ./internal/generate/... -v -race`
- `go test ./internal/prompts/... -v -run TestComposeGenerator`
- `go test ./tests/integration/... -v -run TestGeneratePath` (T401 integration test now exercises the production fan-out)

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate: no retries, no JSON repair, no fail-open. A subprocess error from any provider fails `Run` (T403 will refine to per-provider `.failed` markers + non-blocking; for THIS task, fail loudly — T403 builds on top).
- Per D46: large prompts (256 KB+) MUST go via stdin. The argv-only path causes `E2BIG` on macOS where `getconf ARG_MAX` is often ~256KB. Stdin keeps prompts unbounded by argv limits.
- Per C5: gemini subprocess must receive `--policy-file` pointing at the on-disk policy TOML. This applies to generators (this task) AND reviewers (Epic B) AND debate (Epic C).
- Per C4: `internal/prompts/generators.go` reads from disk at every call; do NOT cache template bytes. This matches Epic B's reviewer-prompt loader (C4 / S6).
- Reuse Epic B's subprocess plumbing via a small private helper (e.g., a function in `internal/reviewer/subprocess.go` that both reviewer.Spawn and generate.runProvider call). If Epic B did not factor this out, this task adds the helper. Do NOT duplicate the argv-composition or stdin-piping code across packages.
- The gemini fallback to a temporary `prompt-stdin.md` file (per plan §Reviewer Subprocess Contract step 4) is decided in Phase B against the actual gemini CLI; if Epic B added the fallback, this task wires the same fallback for generators.
- Do NOT touch run-team-related files.

title: [T403] Generate output layout: <output_dir>/{provider}/{draft.md,raw.json,stats.json} + <provider>.failed markers (errors loud, non-blocking per provider)
description:
**Source Documents**:
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L162-L162](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L162-L162) — Phase D goal: `cerberus generate` subcommand for create-spec / create-plan / architecture-review / healthcheck multi-model drafts.
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L119-L119](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L119-L119) — `bin/generate` (783 LOC bash) → Replace with `cerberus generate` subcommand (used by create-spec/create-plan skills).
- Plan: [docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L26-L26](docs/2026-05-08-rebuild-plan.md#L26-L26) — Simplification mandate: errors surface loudly (log + non-zero exit); fault tolerance NOT carried forward in v2.0 GA.
- v1 reference: [skills/create-spec/SKILL.md#L446-L470](skills/create-spec/SKILL.md#L446-L470) — Existing skill consumer expects `$OUTPUT_DIR/{claude,codex,gemini}/draft.md` and accepts partial success.
- v1 reference: [skills/healthcheck/SKILL.md#L86-L107](skills/healthcheck/SKILL.md#L86-L107) — Same partial-success contract: skill prints \"only existing draft.md files\".

**Type**: task
**Priority**: P2
**Story**: [Epic D]
**Parallel**: yes (with T402, T404)
**Primary Files**: internal/generate/generate.go, internal/generate/output.go, internal/generate/output_test.go, internal/generate/stats.go, internal/generate/stats_test.go
**Subsystems**: internal/generate
**Dependencies**: T401, T402

**Goal**: Define + implement the per-provider output layout for `cerberus generate`: each provider goroutine writes (a) `<output_dir>/<provider>/draft.md` (verbatim subprocess stdout) on success, (b) `<output_dir>/<provider>/raw.json` (the canonical JSON envelope from the provider CLI when it returns JSON output, otherwise omitted), (c) `<output_dir>/<provider>/stats.json` (lightweight per-provider stats: tokens-used, time-to-finish-ms, cost-usd, exit-code, started_at, ended_at), (d) `<output_dir>/<provider>.failed` marker file (touched when that provider's subprocess fails — replaces v1's per-provider failure indicator). Failure semantics are loud-but-non-blocking PER PROVIDER: a single provider's failure does NOT abort the other generators (this matches existing v1 SKILL.md consumer behavior, which already handles 1-of-3 or 2-of-3 successes); the orchestrator returns a non-zero exit code only if ALL providers failed; partial success returns 0 with stderr summary listing which providers failed.

**Context**: The skill consumers under `skills/{create-spec,create-plan,healthcheck,architecture-review}/SKILL.md` (existing v1 documented) already select `<output_dir>/{provider}/draft.md` files that exist and skip ones that don't. T402's loud-fail-all-providers behavior would be a regression for these skills (a single provider crash would block the other 2 from being usable). This task adds per-provider isolation: each goroutine catches its own subprocess error, writes a `<provider>.failed` marker + a `stats.json` with the error, and lets the other goroutines complete. The orchestrator joins all results, prints a stderr summary, and returns 0 unless ALL three failed. This matches the simplification mandate's spirit (errors surface loudly via stderr + the marker file; nothing is silently masked) while preserving the actual user-visible workflow that v1 enables. Per simplification mandate, no retries, no fall-back to a different model, no JSON repair — failures are recorded loudly.

**Scope**:
- In: replace T402's `errgroup.Wait()` failure semantics with per-goroutine catch-and-record. Each goroutine writes one of: success → `draft.md` + `raw.json` (if applicable) + `stats.json`; failure → `<output_dir>/<provider>.failed` (note: at the parent level, not nested under the provider dir, matching v1 marker placement) + `<output_dir>/<provider>/stats.json` with `exit_code` and `error_message`.
- In: `internal/generate/output.go` exposing `WriteSuccess(outputDir, provider string, stdout []byte, rawJSON []byte) error` and `WriteFailure(outputDir, provider string, exitCode int, errMsg string) error` and `WriteStats(outputDir, provider string, stats Stats) error`.
- In: `internal/generate/stats.go` defining the `Stats` struct (`Tokens *TokenStats`, `CostUSD *float64`, `TimeToFinishMs int64`, `ExitCode int`, `ErrorMessage string`, `StartedAt time.Time`, `EndedAt time.Time`); `ParseProviderJSON(provider string, stdout []byte) (rawJSON []byte, stats Stats, err error)` extracts `tokens` + `cost_usd` from each provider's JSON envelope when present.
- In: orchestrator returns non-zero ONLY when all three providers failed; partial success (1-of-3, 2-of-3) returns 0 with a stderr summary `\"cerberus generate: 1 provider succeeded, 2 failed (claude.failed, gemini.failed)\"`.
- In: tests covering: (a) all-three success: 3 `draft.md` + 3 `stats.json` + 0 `.failed` markers; (b) 1-of-3 success: 1 `draft.md` + 3 `stats.json` + 2 `.failed` markers, exit 0; (c) all-three failure: 0 `draft.md` + 3 `stats.json` + 3 `.failed` markers, exit non-zero; (d) `raw.json` written when provider returns parseable JSON; omitted when stdout is plain markdown (e.g., a Claude `--print` non-JSON output).
- Out: full CLI flag surface (`--skip-interview`, `--focus`) (T404); per-`--type` integration coverage (T405); embedded prompts (D40 — N/A here, prompts read from disk per T402).

**Changes**:
- `internal/generate/output.go` — [New] — `WriteSuccess`, `WriteFailure`, `WriteStats` writers; per-provider `os.MkdirAll(<output_dir>/<provider>, 0755)` before any write; `<provider>.failed` marker is `os.WriteFile(<output_dir>/<provider>.failed, []byte(errMsg), 0644)`.
- `internal/generate/stats.go` — [New] — `Stats` struct; `ParseProviderJSON` provider-specific (claude: `{usage: {input_tokens, output_tokens}}`; codex: `{usage: ...}`; gemini: `{usage: ...}`); falls back to zero stats if JSON not present (markdown stdout).
- `internal/generate/generate.go` — [Modify] — Replace T402's `errgroup` join with per-goroutine catch: each goroutine wraps its subprocess+write in a defer-recover-style block; on error, calls `WriteFailure` + `WriteStats` with the error; on success, calls `WriteSuccess` + `WriteStats`. Aggregate result: counts succeeded/failed; if `failed == 3`, return non-zero error; else log summary to stderr and return nil.
- `internal/generate/output_test.go` — [New] — Tests for each writer; correct file paths; correct file contents; idempotent overwrites.
- `internal/generate/stats_test.go` — [New] — Tests for `ParseProviderJSON` for each provider's JSON envelope; tests for plain-markdown fallback (zero stats).
- `internal/generate/generate_test.go` — [Modify] — New cases: 1-of-3 success returns nil; all-failure returns non-zero; `.failed` markers placed correctly; `stats.json` always written.

**Wiring Map**: `internal/generate.Run → fan-out goroutines (T402) → per-goroutine: try { subprocess + WriteSuccess + WriteStats } catch { WriteFailure + WriteStats } → join; if all-failed: return error; else: stderr summary + return nil`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: Output layout test: success run produces `<output_dir>/{claude,codex,gemini}/{draft.md,stats.json}` and zero `.failed` markers.
- AC2: Partial-failure test: 1-of-3 success produces `<output_dir>/{provider-success}/{draft.md,stats.json}` PLUS `<output_dir>/{provider-fail-1,provider-fail-2}/stats.json` (with non-zero `exit_code`) PLUS `<output_dir>/{provider-fail-1.failed,provider-fail-2.failed}` markers; `Run` returns nil; stderr contains a summary.
- AC3: All-failure test: 0 `draft.md`, 3 `stats.json`, 3 `.failed` markers; `Run` returns a non-zero error.

**Verification**:
- `go test ./internal/generate/... -v -run TestOutput`
- `go test ./internal/generate/... -v -run TestStats`
- `go test ./internal/generate/... -v -run TestRunPartialFailure`
- Manual: induce a mock CLI failure (set `CERBERUS_FIXTURE_DIR` to nonexistent for one provider); confirm 2-of-3 succeed and `Run` returns 0.

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate: no retries, no model fallback, no JSON repair. A failed provider stays failed; the marker file + stats record the failure; downstream skills (create-spec/create-plan/healthcheck/architecture-review) handle partial success the same way v1 already does (they print only existing `draft.md` files).
- The `.failed` marker file is placed at `<output_dir>/<provider>.failed` (parent-level, sibling to the `<provider>/` directory), matching v1 placement. Skill consumers grep for these markers to detect failed providers.
- The orchestrator-level non-zero exit ONLY fires when all three providers fail. Partial failure is a normal-flow case (the skill consumer documents this expectation).
- Per simplification mandate, the per-provider exception path is the ONLY fault-tolerance accommodation in v2.0 — it preserves v1 user-visible behavior. Do NOT add additional fault-tolerance (retry, fallback model, etc.) — those are v2.x candidates.
- The `raw.json` file is written ONLY when the provider's stdout is JSON-parseable. For Claude `--print` (markdown) output, `raw.json` is omitted; for Codex `--json` and Gemini `--json` output, `raw.json` contains the canonical envelope. `stats.json` is written for ALL outcomes (success or failure).
- Do NOT touch run-team-related files.

**Goal**: Lock the `cerberus generate` CLI flag surface in `internal/cli/generate.go`: required positional `<output_dir>` (created if absent); required `--type` validated against the enum `{create-spec, create-plan, healthcheck, architecture-review}`; optional `--mode <fast|smart|max>` (default `smart`); optional `--prompt-file <path>` (file content becomes the user prompt sent via stdin per D46) OR free-text trailing args (concatenated to form the user prompt) OR `--focus <text>` (healthcheck-specific shorthand merged into the user prompt); optional `--skip-interview` (boolean; suppresses any interview-engine round-trip the v1 generators wired in for create-spec/create-plan; v2 honors the flag by passing it through to the generator template selector). The `--skip-interview` flag corresponds to the create-spec/create-plan interview-engine round-trip (v1 prompts ask clarifying questions before generating; `--skip-interview` short-circuits that). For v2.0 GA per simplification mandate, `--skip-interview` simply selects a non-interview prompt template path (the actual interview-engine logic lives in the on-disk generator templates per C4 — `internal/cli` just passes the flag through to the template selector). Per D18, flag parsing uses stdlib `flag` only, no cobra/urfave.

title: [Review] 1 non-blocking finding from cerberus-rwu.4
description:
## Review Findings

This issue consolidates 1 non-blocking finding from code review.

**Source issue:** cerberus-rwu.4
**Highest priority:** P3

---

### Finding 1: [P3] Double printing of usage and error messages on flag parse failure

**Priority:** P3
**Reviewer:** gemini
**Location:** internal/cli/generate.go:26-29

The standard `flag` package initialized with `ContinueOnError` automatically prints the error and usage string to its configured output (`stderr` here) when flag parsing fails (e.g., on an unknown flag). Because `runGenerate` catches the wrapped error and explicitly calls `fmt.Fprintln(stderr, err)` and `fmt.Fprintln(stderr, generateUsage)` again, the CLI outputs the exact same error and usage text twice. To fix this, you can set `fs.SetOutput(io.Discard)` in `parseGenerateFlags` or adjust the error handling in `runGenerate` to avoid re-printing.

title: [Review] 2 non-blocking findings from cerberus-rwu.3
description:
## Review Findings

This issue consolidates 2 non-blocking findings from code review.

**Source issue:** cerberus-rwu.3
**Highest priority:** P2

---

### Finding 1: [P2] Clear stale output artifacts on successful overwrite

**Priority:** P2
**Reviewer:** codex
**Location:** internal/generate/output.go:15-22

`WriteSuccess` overwrites `draft.md` and optionally writes `raw.json`, but it never removes stale artifacts from an earlier run. Since the CLI accepts an existing output directory, a provider that failed previously and then succeeds will leave `<output_dir>/<provider>.failed` behind, violating the all-success layout and misleading downstream marker checks; similarly, a prior JSON `raw.json` remains when the new stdout is markdown and `rawJSON` is empty.

---

### Finding 2: [P2] Handle Codex JSONL output when parsing provider stats

**Priority:** P2
**Reviewer:** codex
**Location:** internal/generate/stats.go:24-28

`ParseProviderJSON` returns immediately unless the entire stdout is one valid JSON value. The existing provider runner invokes Codex with `--json`, and the shared reviewer code already handles that provider as newline-delimited JSON objects, so real Codex JSONL stdout will take this fallback path and produce no `raw.json` and no token stats even though the provider returned JSON usage data.

---

**Story**: [Epic A]
**Parallel**: [P]
**Primary Files**: internal/config/config.go, internal/config/config_test.go
**Subsystems**: internal/config
**Dependencies**: T101

**Goal**: Implement the `CERBERUS_*` env-var resolver as a first-class Go package, with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` honored as the single fallback for `CERBERUS_ROOT`. v1's `REVIEW_GATE_*` aliases are NOT supported.

**Context**: R7 binds the env contract: v2 reads `CERBERUS_ROOT, CERBERUS_HOST, CERBERUS_RUN_KEY, CERBERUS_SESSION_ID, CERBERUS_STATE_ROOT, CERBERUS_PROJECT_KEY, CERBERUS_TRANSCRIPT_PATH`. C2 fixes the simplification posture: no env aliases, no fallbacks beyond `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT → CERBERUS_ROOT`. This package is consumed by every CLI subcommand and hook handler so it lands early in Epic A.

**Scope**:
- In: `internal/config.Env` struct holding all spec-bound env values; `internal/config.Resolve()` that reads `os.Getenv` for each var, applies the `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT → CERBERUS_ROOT` fallback, and returns the populated struct; unit tests covering happy path + each missing-var scenario.
- Out: host detection (T103); state-root derivation (Epic B `internal/state`); session-id minting (Epic B); reviewer-CLI flags.

**Changes**:
- `internal/config/config.go` — [New] — `Env` struct with one field per spec env var; `Resolve() *Env` reads env; CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT fallback applied only for CERBERUS_ROOT (no other aliases).
- `internal/config/config_test.go` — [New] — Tests: (a) all CERBERUS_* set → struct fields populated verbatim; (b) CERBERUS_ROOT unset + CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT set → CERBERUS_ROOT resolves to CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT; (c) REVIEW_GATE_ROOT set + CERBERUS_ROOT unset → CERBERUS_ROOT remains empty (no v1 alias support).

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- AC1: `Resolve()` returns an `Env` struct whose `Root` field equals `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` when `CERBERUS_ROOT` is unset, per R7 verification ("`CERBERUS_ROOT` unset and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` set → `CERBERUS_ROOT` resolves to the `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` value").
- AC2: Unit test verifies that setting only `REVIEW_GATE_ROOT` does NOT populate `Env.Root` (C2 simplification mandate).

**Verification**:
- `go test ./internal/config/...`
- `go vet ./internal/config/...`

**Notes for Agent**:
- Per simplification mandate: do NOT support `REVIEW_GATE_*` aliases. Errors are loud (empty fields, callers must handle).
- Keep the package surface minimal — Env struct + Resolve constructor. No setters, no merging, no defaults beyond the documented CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT fallback.
- This package is consumed by `internal/cli` (T101) as a parameter threaded through subcommand handlers, per plan §Architecture.

**Context**: R6 mandates the test matrix runs against `CERBERUS_HOST={claude,codex,generic}`. The host adapter is the abstraction that lets the orchestrator and hook layers stay host-neutral while the on-disk state tree differs per host (Claude lives under `~/.claude/projects/<project_key>/cerberus/`; Codex under `~/.codex/projects/<project_key>/cerberus/`; generic uses `${CERBERUS_STATE_ROOT}` per plan §State Tree Layout state-derivation rules). **Scope**:
- In: `internal/host.Adapter` interface (`Name()`, `StateRoot(env)`, `ProjectKey(env)` minimally); three implementations claude/codex/generic; constructor `NewFromEnv(env *config.Env) (Adapter, error)` that selects based on `CERBERUS_HOST`; unit tests for each adapter's state-root + project-key derivation.
- Out: hook payload parsing (lives in `internal/hook` Epic B); session-init logic (Epic B + E); reviewer subprocess (Epic B).

**Changes**:
- `internal/host/host.go` — [New] — `Adapter` interface + claude/codex/generic implementations; project-key = `sha256(absRepoPath)[0:16]`; state-root per-host as documented in plan.

- Do NOT touch hook handlers or run-team files.

### Finding 1: [P2] Missing .PHONY declaration for non-file targets

**Priority:** P2
**Reviewer:** gemini
**Location:** Makefile:4-21

The Makefile is missing a `.PHONY` declaration for standard non-file targets (`build`, `install`, `test`, `lint`, `fixtures-refresh`). Because targets like `test`, `lint`, and `install` have no prerequisites, if a file or directory matching any of these names is ever created in the repository root (e.g., a `test` directory), Make will consider the target up-to-date and skip executing its recipe entirely.

title: [Review] 1 non-blocking finding from cerberus-yd7.6
description:
## Review Findings

This issue consolidates 1 non-blocking finding from code review.

**Source issue:** cerberus-yd7.6
**Highest priority:** P2

---

### Finding 1: [P2] `firstLine` crashes test on empty files with `io.EOF`

**Priority:** P2
**Reviewer:** gemini
**Location:** tests/integration/cleanup_invariants_test.go:196-198

When reading an empty file, `file.Read` returns `n=0` and `err=io.EOF`. The `firstLine` function treats this as a read error and returns `io.EOF`, causing the caller to crash the test (`t.Fatalf("read first line of ...: EOF")`) instead of properly concluding the file has no shebang. Empty files are valid readable files and should not trigger a fatal I/O error that aborts the rest of the shebang checks. Update the condition to `if err != nil && err != io.EOF`.

---

title: [Review] 2 non-blocking findings from cerberus-yd7.7
description:
## Review Findings

This issue consolidates 2 non-blocking findings from code review.

**Source issue:** cerberus-yd7.7
**Highest priority:** P2

---

### Finding 1: [P2] Preserve resolver bytes in extraction helper

**Priority:** P2
**Reviewer:** codex
**Location:** tests/integration/skill_bootstrap_drift_test.go:49

The drift detector is intended to compare resolver regions byte-for-byte, but this helper trims the extracted region before returning it. When T601 compares `ExtractResolverBody(canonical)` to each embedded bootstrap, leading/trailing blank lines or missing boundary whitespace around the resolver region will be silently normalized instead of reported as drift, so the test can pass even when the embedded region is not byte-identical to the canonical source.

---

### Finding 2: [P3] Unreachable empty body check in ExtractResolverBody

**Priority:** P3
**Reviewer:** gemini
**Location:** tests/integration/skill_bootstrap_drift_test.go:50-52

The `if body == ""` check is unreachable dead code. Because `input[start : start+end]` starts exactly at `resolverStartMarker`, the extracted `body` inherently includes the 74-character start marker and thus will never be empty. If the intent was to extract only the content *between* the markers and check if that is empty, `start` should be incremented by `len(resolverStartMarker)` before slicing.

---

## Review Findings

### Finding 1: [P3] Document make as always required for Codex hooks

**Priority:** P3
**Reviewer:** codex
**Location:** docs/CODEX.md:129-130

This troubleshooting bullet says either `bin/cerberus` exists or `make`/Go are available, but every command in `hooks/codex-hooks.json` runs `command -v make` before checking whether the build is current or executing `bin/cerberus`. A user with a valid prebuilt `bin/cerberus` but no `make` on the hook runner PATH will still get `cerberus: make not found on PATH`, so this points them at the wrong fix.
